CAP-233-CS-01. Given: Inline design crashes after commit without a durable intent
Expected: Record the missing dispatch intent for cs-app1; do not invent an undeclared recovery scanner.
State: PROPOSED_EXPECTATION_NOT_OBSERVED. Fresh named fixture state, counters and fixed clock per case unless an explicit sequence is stated.

CAP-233-CS-02. Given: Outbox design crashes and recovers with duplicate transport delivery
Expected: Retain intent and apply the receiver effect at most once per business key; record rows, sends and effects without claiming globally exactly-once delivery.
State: PROPOSED_EXPECTATION_NOT_OBSERVED. Fresh named fixture state, counters and fixed clock per case unless an explicit sequence is stated.

CAP-233-CS-03. Given: Reviewed revision changes or cancellation wins before the dispatch claim
Expected: Block stale dispatch; a transport replay epoch never authorizes a second policy or economic effect.
State: PROPOSED_EXPECTATION_NOT_OBSERVED. Fresh named fixture state, counters and fixed clock per case unless an explicit sequence is stated.

days.practical_task: CAP-234 · Day 227 · 2027-05-28 · Rehearse one timed product code change

CAP-235-CS-02. Given: Any class fails, is not run, belongs to another candidate or has incompatible restore evidence

CAP-235-CS-05. Given: Analytics reports payment success but server payment/audit state is UNKNOWN, or encryption key is unavailable after process restart
Expected: Keep the authoritative unknown/reconciliation state and HOLD the applicable readiness class. Browser observations never create a paid state; missing key is KEY_UNAVAILABLE, not a successful empty restore.
State: PROPOSED_EXPECTATION_NOT_OBSERVED. Fresh named fixture state, counters and fixed clock per case unless an explicit sequence is stated.

days.primary_title: Day 229 · 30 May 2027 — Fence a revoked Support history read (150m)
days.practical_task: Against the exact Phase 1 candidate, author one read-authorization test and the smallest boundary rule that prevents a history result from being released after its assignment is revoked.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- U at unchanged generation 10 receives E1; V receives the same safe denial as an unknown case.
- Release R after generation 11: no history body or PRIVATE-A reaches U; record the observed rejection point.
- Unauthorized requests call decrypt and provider ports zero times; a UUID alone never establishes scope.

days.primary_title: Day 230 · 31 May 2027 — Make history scope values immutable (150m)
days.practical_task: Design and implement an immutable Java scope value used to select case-history records, including equality, hash behavior and defensive copying of event-kind filters.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- S1 and S2 compare equal and occupy one hash-set entry after documented set normalization.
- Changing the caller list cannot alter S1 or its hash; exposed accessors cannot mutate its contents.
- S3 remains distinct; case and actor identifiers are never normalized into shared authority.

days.primary_title: Day 231 · 01 Jun 2027 — Order tied history events deterministically (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement an immutable history comparator that respects authoritative sequence and provides a total deterministic order for a bounded merged display fixture.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Normal output is E1, E2, E3 regardless of timestamp order; exact E2 replay is handled once.
- E2 b is reported as conflicting authoritative identity rather than silently winning by timestamp.
- Comparator antisymmetry/transitivity hold over all permutations of E1–E3; inputs remain unchanged.

days.primary_title: Day 232 · 02 Jun 2027 — Model history failures as typed outcomes (150m)
days.practical_task: Create a Java result boundary for history loading that distinguishes unavailable data, malformed request and denied/unknown resource without leaking internal exceptions.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Valid C1 maps to a page and pageSize 0 maps to invalid-filter before database access.
- C9 and foreign C2 have indistinguishable safe response shape; JDBC-PRIVATE-A never appears in outward output.
- Temporary unavailability is not converted to an empty successful page; every declared outcome is handled.

days.primary_title: Day 233 · 03 Jun 2027 — Constrain generic history projections (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one typed Java projection helper for immutable events that cannot accidentally erase source provenance or accept a mutable domain entity as a public DTO.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Both event types produce the same bounded display shape with their original source identity/revision intact.
- The chosen API rejects or explicitly validates the missing-revision projector; no unchecked cast hides the mismatch.
- Returned DTOs contain no mutable persistence entity or protected payload reference that bypasses access checks.

days.primary_title: Day 234 · 04 Jun 2027 — Parse bounded case-history filters (150m)
days.practical_task: Write the Java parser and normalized filter value for one read-only history request, including limits and mutually consistent cursor options.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Valid query yields exactly two unique allowed kinds, ascending order and limit 2; duplicate identical kinds normalize once.
- Unknown kind and out-of-range limits are rejected before data access.
- Cursor plus reset=true is rejected rather than silently reusing a stale fence; normalized equality matches day 2.

days.primary_title: Day 235 · 05 Jun 2027 — Strengthen scope-key regression examples (150m)
days.practical_task: Add learner-authored regression cases that expose a scope-key implementation omitting assignment generation or conflating empty and absent filters; repair only that key seam.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Generation 10 and 11 produce distinct keys; the cached old page cannot satisfy a new-generation lookup.
- Absent filter normalizes to the documented all-kinds value; explicit empty filter fails validation.
- Reordering the same allowed kinds still reuses one key, without dropping actor or case identity.

days.primary_title: Day 236 · 06 Jun 2027 — Close failed history resource reads (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one bounded Java read adapter whose resource lifetime remains correct when mapping the third record fails.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Successful read returns three events and closes the cursor exactly once.
- Malformed E3 produces no successful partial page and closes exactly once.
- MAP_ERROR remains primary with CLOSE_ERROR retained as suppressed safe diagnostic information; outward error contains neither raw row nor private marker.

days.primary_title: Day 237 · 07 Jun 2027 — Resolve exact source revisions safely (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a read-only source-reference resolver for a history event that requires an exact source type, object and revision before producing a navigable reference.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- E1 resolves revision 2 even though revision 3 exists.
- Missing revision 4 produces source-unavailable, not revision 3; RAW_PROVIDER is rejected.
- V gets no source lookup or decrypt call; resolution never changes source records or policy/payment authority.

days.primary_title: Day 238 · 08 Jun 2027 — Model a captured history fence (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a pure Java pagination model that captures the current authoritative sequence fence and advances only within that fence.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Pages are [1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]; final continuation is absent.
- Sequence 7 never enters this chain and appears after deliberate refresh captures fence 7.
- Mismatched case or generation invalidates the cursor; every returned sequence is greater than its cursor position and no greater than the fence.

days.primary_title: Day 239 · 09 Jun 2027 — Diagnose a mutable filter map key (150m)
days.practical_task: Use a failing lookup to isolate caller mutation of a Java map key, then repair the smallest value boundary with a regression.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The original fixture reproduces a lost lookup without database or network calls.
- After repair, mutating the caller list leaves the original lookup stable and hash unchanged.
- C2 cannot retrieve C1 data; the fix does not globally disable key equality or cache use.

days.primary_title: Day 240 · 10 Jun 2027 — Bound duplicate history normalization (150m)
days.practical_task: Design a single-pass normalizer for at most 100 read-model rows that removes exact duplicate event identities while rejecting contradictory duplicates.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Normal result is E1, E2, E3 in authoritative order with exact duplicate count 1.
- Conflicting E2 fails the page rather than selecting a winner; 101 rows fail before an unbounded allocation path.
- Input is unchanged and source identity survives normalization; duplicate suppression creates no new audit or money effects.

days.primary_title: Day 241 · 11 Jun 2027 — Separate audit history from click events (150m)
days.practical_task: Write a projection reducer that admits only authoritative domain/audit records and handles unknown/reconciled outcomes without deriving business truth from browser analytics.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- PENDING, UNKNOWN, RECONCILED_SUCCEEDED remain visible in sequence; the click is excluded.
- M1 is referenced once as an effect with amountMinor=12500 and currency=INR, without summing repeated observations into amountMinor=25000, currency=INR.
- Dropping all analytics leaves the same authoritative history and causes zero payment/provider commands.

days.primary_title: Day 242 · 12 Jun 2027 — Reconstruct a history access contract (150m)
days.practical_task: From a plain decision table with no implementation outline, recreate one executable history-access predicate that handles owner, assigned Support and unknown source revision.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Exactly the owner A/C1 and assigned U/C1 rows permit lookup.
- Missing revision 4 is source-unavailable after authorized access; it is never replaced by a newer source.
- Denied and unknown cases reveal no case fields and make zero decrypt/provider calls; no copied prior predicate counts as independent evidence.

days.primary_title: Day 243 · 13 Jun 2027 — Coordinate read release with revocation (150m)
days.practical_task: Choose and implement one concurrency protocol for the Support authorization/read-release seam, using a deterministic two-thread schedule and the actual assignment interface.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- When revocation commits first, R releases no private result.
- When read release wins first, the result is documented as authorized at that linearization point, without claiming revocation retracts bytes already sent.
- Both schedules finish within a 2-second test deadline without sleeps as synchronization or provider/decrypt calls.

days.primary_title: Day 244 · 14 Jun 2027 — Publish immutable filter configuration (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement safe publication of a versioned public filter registry used by concurrent history readers, without caching private result data.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Every read observes either the complete V1 pair or complete V2 pair, never V2 kinds with V1 limit.
- Published collections cannot be changed by the writer or reader; no partially built registry is visible.
- Only public enum/configuration data is retained; case pages, user scopes and protected fields are absent.

days.primary_title: Day 245 · 15 Jun 2027 — Bound concurrent history projections (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement admission and rejection handling for one existing local projection executor with two workers and a queue of three.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Exactly two tasks are active and three queued at the controlled full point; task 6 receives explicit unavailable/rejected outcome.
- Releasing latches completes admitted tasks with no lost result and no leaked resource.
- Rejection never falls back to an unbounded queue or executes private work under an unintended caller identity.

days.primary_title: Day 246 · 16 Jun 2027 — Cancel interrupted history work cleanly (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement cooperative deadline/cancellation handling around a bounded history read task and preserve interruption semantics.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Cooperative T stops before row 3 after interruption and closes its resource once.
- Successful control returns all three rows; cancellation is not reported as a successful empty page.
- Interrupt-insensitive fake is reported still-running until explicitly released; evidence does not equate Future cancellation with physical termination.

days.primary_title: Day 247 · 17 Jun 2027 — Expose a bypassed Spring transaction (150m)
days.practical_task: Author an integration test that contrasts self-invocation with proxy-mediated invocation for one existing atomic journey-transition seam, then move only the required public boundary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The initial fixture records whether the expected transaction is active in each call path; no behavior is inferred from annotation presence alone.
- Repaired failure path leaves journey version 4 and no A1 in the actual database.
- Successful path commits version 5 and exactly one A1 together; provider-call count remains 0.

days.primary_title: Day 248 · 18 Jun 2027 — Regress checked-exception rollback rules (150m)
days.practical_task: Extend the transaction boundary with tests for one checked validation exception and one unchecked failure, choosing an explicit rollback rule for the actual installed stack.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Both designated rollback failures leave version 4 and audit count 0 in committed database state.
- The catch-and-return variant is shown to be unsafe unless it explicitly marks rollback or moves validation before writes; learner proves the chosen repair.
- Valid O1 commits once; test transactions are not allowed to conceal application-level commit behavior.

days.primary_title: Day 249 · 19 Jun 2027 — Keep required audit in one transaction (150m)
days.practical_task: Compare REQUIRED and REQUIRES_NEW for one mandatory audit write and choose the propagation that preserves domain/audit atomicity.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The REQUIRES_NEW variant demonstrates whether A2 survives the outer rollback in the actual database.
- Selected production seam leaves neither state change nor required A2 after failure and commits both on success.
- Lossy analytics remains separate; it is never used to justify an orphaned required audit event.

days.primary_title: Day 250 · 20 Jun 2027 — Validate cross-field history requests (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one Spring request validator for date range, page limit and continuation compatibility, mapping its domain errors without leaking rejected raw values.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Seven-day range is accepted and retains half-open endpoint semantics.
- Each invalid combination fails before repository invocation; unrecognized privateField is rejected rather than reflected.
- Outward errors expose field codes only, contain no SECRET-A and preserve the same authorization checks as valid requests.

days.primary_title: Day 251 · 21 Jun 2027 — Isolate identities on pooled threads (150m)
days.practical_task: Diagnose and repair one SecurityContext propagation/cleanup seam in asynchronous read-only history projection.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Task A sees U; task B sees V and is denied; task 3 is unauthenticated.
- After task A throws, reused worker retains no U context; cleanup is verified rather than inferred from a finally block.
- No principal is copied into persistent cache or logs, and V/anonymous tasks make zero private-data calls.

days.primary_title: Day 252 · 22 Jun 2027 — Authorize every batched history reference (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one bounded batch-read service that preserves input correspondence and scope checks for each case reference rather than authorizing only the first.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Result contains C1 once with E1, E2; C2 and C9 have indistinguishable unavailable entries.
- No C2/C9 private lookup or decrypt occurs; authorizing C1 cannot authorize the rest of the batch.
- Five references reject before fan-out, and exact duplicate C1 does not multiply queries or effects.

days.primary_title: Day 253 · 23 Jun 2027 — Diagnose an escaped lazy projection (150m)
days.practical_task: Minimize a seeded lazy-loading failure where a history DTO accesses an ORM relation after its transaction ends, then repair the read projection boundary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Baseline reproduces the unavailable-lazy-state failure or documents actual installed behavior with query traces.
- Repaired response serializes all three references with no database access after service return.
- C1 query count stays within the learner-declared bounded projection count; no global open-session workaround or protected payload serialization is introduced.

days.primary_title: Day 254 · 24 Jun 2027 — Separate provider observation from SQL work (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one result-recording boundary for an existing mock operation so the external mock call occurs outside the SQL transaction and an unknown result keeps its durable reference.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Mock call observes no active SQL transaction and uses the already durable O3 reference.
- Result-recording rollback leaves the prior pending/unknown reference for reconciliation, not a falsely committed success audit.
- Definite failure commits FAILED plus required audit together; retries never create an extra effect with amountMinor=12500 and currency=INR.

days.primary_title: Day 255 · 25 Jun 2027 — Resolve simultaneous journey version writes (150m)
days.practical_task: Design and execute a two-writer optimistic-concurrency test against one existing synthetic journey command, including the precise losing response.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Exactly one operation commits version 5 with one matching audit and step event; the loser is an explicit version conflict.
- No version 6 or orphan loser audit appears; the resulting step matches the winner.
- Repeating with reversed release order changes the possible winner but never permits both; record real database evidence.

days.primary_title: Day 256 · 26 Jun 2027 — Choose a consistent two-record lock order (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement and test canonical lock ordering for one existing synthetic operation that touches two permitted records, using bounded opposing request orders.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Baseline shows a detected deadlock or bounded lock timeout with captured transaction outcome, never a hanging test.
- Ordered variant acquires records in the same stable order and both permitted operations terminate.
- A failed transaction leaves no partial versions/audit; unauthorized record identifiers are denied before locks on private records.

days.primary_title: Day 257 · 27 Jun 2027 — Map transaction failures without false success (150m)
days.practical_task: Write one exception-to-response mapper that distinguishes stale version, bounded contention and unknown mock outcome while preserving safe diagnostics.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Stale version asks for a fresh authoritative read; it is never blindly retried as an unchanged write.
- Unknown O3 remains pending-reconciliation rather than FAILED or successful empty data.
- All errors omit SQL-SECRET and private SQL/credentials; any suggested retry is bounded and preserves durable operation identity.

days.primary_title: Day 258 · 28 Jun 2027 — Measure bounded executor saturation (150m)
days.practical_task: Run a small local comparison of the day 17 executor under two declared queue limits and use observed admission/latency/resource evidence to retain one configuration.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- For every run, submitted 20 equals completed+rejected+cancelled+still-running at the stated cutoff; no failures vanish from latency reporting.
- Maximum active<=2 and observed queue<=selected capacity; all resources close after drain.
- Decision states real measured trade-offs and environment limits; no fixture wait times are presented as production capacity or a guaranteed speedup.

days.primary_title: Day 259 · 29 Jun 2027 — Preserve operation identity under duplicate calls (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one concurrent durable-operation claim seam that distinguishes an exact duplicate request from reuse of the same key with changed revision.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Exact concurrent requests reference one durable operation and at most one claimed mock invocation/effect.
- Changed revision 3 under K1 returns conflict without mutating revision 2 acceptance.
- Database rollback/retry preserves existing operation identity and one immutable effect with amountMinor=12500 and currency=INR; in-memory deduplication alone is insufficient evidence.

days.primary_title: Day 260 · 30 Jun 2027 — Expose an atomic transition to history (150m)
days.practical_task: Complete one read-projection integration seam so a committed existing journey transition appears in Support history only with its matching authoritative audit/source reference.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Committed control exposes seq 4 with exact A6 and revision 2; version 5, audit and step event agree.
- Failed transaction exposes no seq 4 or A6 and leaves version 4; no partial history appears.
- Projection is read-only and makes no provider/decrypt calls; analytics availability has no effect on returned rows.

days.primary_title: Day 261 · 01 Jul 2027 — Design history projection keys and constraints (150m)
days.practical_task: Design and execute the smallest disposable relational projection schema for case-history references, preserving existing event/source identity instead of creating another business ledger.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- C1/seq 1 and C2/seq 1 coexist; duplicate(C1, seq 2) fails.
- Sequence 0 and incomplete application source reference fail under the declared constraints or one explicitly identified application-level rule.
- Original ApplicationRevision composite identity is retained; projection changes create no business audit/money effects.

days.primary_title: Day 262 · 02 Jul 2027 — Prove nullable source constraint behavior (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement and test one conditional source-reference constraint that correctly handles SQL UNKNOWN rather than relying on a CHECK that accidentally passes nulls.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- APPLICATION/revision 2 with sourceId A1 succeeds; NULL and 0 fail.
- SYSTEM_NOTICE with absent source fields succeeds and with sourceId A1 fails.
- Unknown event/source type is rejected; passing a CHECK due to UNKNOWN cannot admit a malformed source reference.

days.primary_title: Day 263 · 03 Jul 2027 — Prevent assignment joins from multiplying events (150m)
days.practical_task: Write a scoped history query that admits current assignment without multiplying history rows when historical assignment records exist.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- U/C1 gets exactly 3 rows, not 6; each eventId appears once.
- U/C2 and V/C1 return zero private rows despite valid identifiers.
- Adding another revoked assignment does not change cardinality or grant access; query logic explains why.

days.primary_title: Day 264 · 04 Jul 2027 — Count empty histories and unknown outcomes (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one aggregate projection that includes authorized cases with no events and separates unknown observations from confirmed money effects.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- C1 observation count 4, unknown count 1 and distinct confirmed effect sum amountMinor=12500, currency=INR are reported separately.
- C2 remains present with counts 0 and the documented zero confirmed total; COUNT(*) on a left-join placeholder must not report 1.
- C3 contributes nothing; duplicate observation of M1 never doubles money and currencies are never silently summed together.

days.primary_title: Day 265 · 05 Jul 2027 — Implement fenced SQL keyset pages (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement the actual scoped PostgreSQL keyset query matching day 10’s page model, with an explicit fence and bounded page size.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Pages return [1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6] and no continuation after 6.
- Appended 7 is excluded until new refresh captures 7; duplicate timestamps cause neither skips nor duplicates.
- U cannot change case to C2 or reuse an unauthorized scope; all returned sequences are within(lastSequence, fence].

days.primary_title: Day 266 · 06 Jul 2027 — Reconstruct a mixed-scope history query (150m)
days.practical_task: Recreate a scoped keyset query from the input/output contract in a blank query seam, using an unfamiliar assignment history and no prior SQL pasted in.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- U/C4 returns [4, 6] exactly; sequence 8 lies beyond the fence.
- V/C4 and U/C5 expose zero rows even though identifiers exist.
- An added duplicate historical assignment does not duplicate results; evidence distinguishes independent construction from referenced prior solutions.

days.primary_title: Day 267 · 07 Jul 2027 — Bind continuation cursors to query meaning (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one cursor-validation/SQL-parameter adapter using the existing approved opaque cursor codec, binding scope, filters, direction and fence.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Matching cursor yields the intended continuation after 2 through 6.
- Every semantic mismatch and last 7>fence 6 rejects before the history query; malformed input returns a safe invalid-cursor outcome.
- Fresh server authorization still occurs for matching cursors, and any cryptographic verification stays in the existing maintained codec.

days.primary_title: Day 268 · 08 Jul 2027 — Specify null-aware history summaries (150m)
days.practical_task: Write a deterministic SQL display projection for optional source labels while keeping authoritative ordering entirely sequence-based.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- E1/E2 use the documented fallback while retaining exact original references.
- E3 is typed as source-free system notice, not a falsely resolved application source.
- Changing labels, including null/empty, cannot reorder sequences 1–3 or silently change a source revision.

days.primary_title: Day 269 · 09 Jul 2027 — Test a fence against concurrent source edits (150m)
days.practical_task: Run a two-connection MVCC experiment to define what the history fence does and does not freeze, then choose immutable event snapshot fields for the read contract.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Append 7 stays outside the fenced chain regardless of label visibility.
- Evidence records whether page 2 sees NEW; it does not falsely claim the fence freezes mutable joined fields.
- Selected history contract uses immutable revision-bound label data or explicitly labels current display data; source identity and sequence remain unchanged.

days.primary_title: Day 270 · 10 Jul 2027 — Observe a blocked history transaction (150m)
days.practical_task: Capture and explain one bounded lock wait involving the history source, then shorten only the unnecessary transaction lifetime in the read adapter.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Blocked fixture identifies blocker and waiter with exact transaction timing and bounded failure.
- Control projection reads permitted committed fields without the unnecessary lock or falsely observing uncommitted data.
- All sessions finish/rollback after the test; no retained open transaction or authority weakening is accepted as a fix.

days.primary_title: Day 271 · 11 Jul 2027 — Diagnose a lost empty-case aggregate (150m)
days.practical_task: Find why a seeded left-join aggregate drops an authorized case with no matching events, then repair predicate placement with a minimal fixture.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Baseline returns C1 only, demonstrating the lost C2 rather than an empty database.
- Repair returns(C1, 1), (C2, 0) and no C3.
- Adding CLOSED to C2 keeps its OPENED count 0 and keeps C2 present; ownership predicate still restricts the case side.

days.primary_title: Day 272 · 12 Jul 2027 — Explain a fixed history query plan (150m)
days.practical_task: Generate and interpret an actual PostgreSQL plan for one scoped keyset query on fixed synthetic data, comparing estimates to actual rows without changing indexes yet.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All runs return sequences 51–70 and no other case; 20 rows is the output oracle.
- Report actual/estimated rows, loops, scan/join types and buffers when supported by the installed version.
- Separate planner/execution observations from end-user latency; a sequential scan can be a justified outcome and no speedup is claimed.

days.primary_title: Day 273 · 13 Jul 2027 — Compare one justified history index (150m)
days.practical_task: Use day 44’s hypothesis to compare the existing index with at most one candidate index in a disposable fixture, then retain or reject it from matched observations.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Both variants return identical sequences 51–70 and preserve source/scope constraints.
- Comparison includes index definition/size and actual query observations; unsupported timing differences are labeled inconclusive.
- Decision addresses maintenance cost and existing prefix coverage; no production migration or promised performance gain follows automatically.

days.primary_title: Day 274 · 14 Jul 2027 — Evolve a nullable projection field safely (150m)
days.practical_task: Prepare and execute one additive schema change for an optional safe summary code on the disposable read projection, including old-writer/new-reader compatibility.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Old writer still inserts E3; new reader displays a documented safe fallback for NULL.
- E4 preserves its allowlisted code; an arbitrary value SECRET-A is rejected by the chosen validation boundary.
- Migration changes only the derived read projection, not immutable business event identity, money effects or exact accepted revisions.

days.primary_title: Day 275 · 15 Jul 2027 — Backfill derived summaries in bounded batches (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one resumable, idempotent backfill for the new derived summary code using bounded keyset batches and no rewrites of authoritative events.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- First batch touches at most 2 rows; resume eventually fills all eligible NULL codes.
- Concurrent valid seq 3 is not overwritten; repeating the completed backfill changes 0 rows.
- Authoritative audit/event/source/money rows are byte/value unchanged, and progress receipts contain no protected payloads.

days.primary_title: Day 276 · 16 Jul 2027 — Measure offset versus fenced keyset work (150m)
days.practical_task: Compare offset and keyset access to the same late history page with real plans and exact result equality, then explain where each approach fits.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Both variants return sequences 19001–19020 with identical source references.
- Record actual scanned/filtered rows, buffers where supported, execution times and failures for every run.
- Explain observed work and limitations without extrapolating to production or forcing an index change; ownership still applies in both queries.

days.primary_title: Day 277 · 17 Jul 2027 — Retry one serialization failure safely (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a bounded transaction retry around one disposable projection-update operation, reopening the transaction for each retry and preserving operation identity.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Observed serialization failure is retried in a new transaction at most once; actual SQLSTATE/outcome are recorded.
- Nonretryable invalid-source fails after one attempt; exhausted retry returns explicit unavailable/conflict rather than success.
- No duplicate projection effect or audit identity appears, and no external mock call is repeated inside the retry.

days.primary_title: Day 278 · 18 Jul 2027 — Map SQL pages into the history contract (150m)
days.practical_task: Complete one SQL-to-Java read adapter for the fenced history page, checking row shape, continuation and safe missing-source representation.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- First page has seq 1, 2 and continuation last 2/fence 3; second has seq 3 and no continuation.
- Malformed projected rows fail safely rather than entering the UI as valid data; missing label preserves exact source reference.
- V returns no private page; adapter performs no writes, decrypt or provider operations.

days.primary_title: Day 279 · 19 Jul 2027 — Separate history server and draft state (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a small state boundary for the history screen that keeps fetched rows in TanStack Query, applied filters in URL state and unapplied filter edits local.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Background refetch updates rows without overwriting unapplied CLOSED draft.
- Apply changes URL/applied filter once and resets invalid selection; Reset restores draft from current applied state.
- There is no copied competing global row collection and no write/submission triggered by a refetch effect.

days.primary_title: Day 280 · 20 Jul 2027 — Design history query-key factories (150m)
days.practical_task: Author typed query-key/options factories for history pages and details from the day 50 contract, including every result-changing scope/filter/fence input.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Equivalent normalized kind sets reuse one key; pages differing in fence, cursor, limit or scope do not.
- Detail and list namespaces cannot collide; user/case/generation variants remain isolated.
- Key inspection contains no token or protected field, and server authorization still governs every request.

days.primary_title: Day 281 · 21 Jul 2027 — Define truthful history query states (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement the history query’s read retry and display-state policy for pending, empty, unavailable, stale-with-data and authorization failure.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Initial pending shows a named loading state; successful empty shows a distinct empty message.
- 503 uses no more than 2 total attempts; 401/403/decode failure use one attempt and no retry loop.
- Background 503 can retain clearly marked existing data, but authorization loss clears private rows rather than labeling them merely stale.

days.primary_title: Day 282 · 22 Jul 2027 — Carry cancellation into history transport (150m)
days.practical_task: Connect the query-provided AbortSignal to the actual history transport and verify cancellation across an applied-filter change.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Cancelling R1 reaches the actual transport signal and records an abort when the transport cooperates.
- Late noncooperative R1 cannot replace current CLOSED rows; logout removes private in-flight/cache state.
- Cancellation is not shown as successful empty history and creates no automatic mutation or write retry.

days.primary_title: Day 283 · 23 Jul 2027 — Preserve unapplied filters during refresh (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one controlled filter-editor composition that preserves dirty input across server refresh and deliberately reconciles URL changes.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Background fetch leaves CLOSED draft and dirty indicator intact.
- Browser Back follows the declared policy: reset draft to NOTE_ADDED with visible state change, without silently applying CLOSED.
- Cancel restores the current applied filter; only explicit Apply changes the filter URL and no domain command is emitted.

days.primary_title: Day 284 · 24 Jul 2027 — Regress overlapping safe shortlist edits (150m)
days.practical_task: Fix one optimistic-update race in the existing reversible shortlist seam using serialized or operation-aware reconciliation, then write the counterexample independently.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- After M1 failure, confirmed Y remains and final displayed list is [X, Z, Y] after reconciliation.
- No duplicate item or size>3 survives; invalidation touches only the affected shortlist scope.
- Account B never renders A’s pending items or rollback snapshot; no optimistic payment/submission state is introduced.

days.primary_title: Day 285 · 25 Jul 2027 — Normalize history filters in the URL (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement the URL-to-filter adapter for the history explorer with deterministic normalization, safe defaults and explicit invalid-value feedback.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Equivalent kind order serializes canonically and produces the same query key.
- Invalid limits/kinds/conflicting cursors display a safe recoverable invalid-link state without fetching a broadened private query.
- Round-trip preserves only supported navigation values; no token, free-text draft or consumer detail is inserted into the URL.

days.primary_title: Day 286 · 26 Jul 2027 — Reset page chains on filter changes (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement explicit fenced-page navigation that resets continuation when filter or assignment generation changes and captures a new fence only on deliberate refresh.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Next within the unchanged chain retains fence 6 and never shows 7.
- Changing filter/generation clears the old cursor and selection before the first new request; no incompatible request is emitted.
- Explicit Refresh captures fence 7 and starts at the first page; cached old pages cannot be appended to the new chain.

days.primary_title: Day 287 · 27 Jul 2027 — Design a typed history-list composition (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one reusable presentational list composition with finite loading/empty/error/ready states and typed row/action slots, leaving fetching in domain hooks.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All four primary states render meaningful accessible content without ambiguous blank output.
- Invalid mutually exclusive state combinations are unrepresentable or explicitly rejected; UNKNOWN is never labeled success.
- Component performs no fetches or domain mutations and accepts typed source/action slots without importing a domain repository.

days.primary_title: Day 288 · 28 Jul 2027 — Make history row details keyboard usable (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a row disclosure interaction for the shared history list using native controls, stable accessible names and predictable keyboard/focus behavior.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each control has a unique name containing its event context and exposes expanded state/controlled region.
- Enter/Space toggle the intended disclosure and normal Tab order remains predictable; unavailable source is still explainable.
- No custom arrow-key grid or hidden focusable descendants are introduced; source access still uses the authorized resolver.

days.primary_title: Day 289 · 29 Jul 2027 — Constrain focus in the source dialog (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one source-reference detail dialog using the existing dialog primitive, supplying its task-specific focus, dismissal and unavailable-source behavior.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Dialog has a meaningful name, initial focus and contained Tab order; background controls are inert while open.
- Escape/close returns focus to the invoking row when present, otherwise to the documented list heading fallback.
- Unavailable source displays a safe explanation with a close action; it neither fetches latest revision nor leaves focus lost.

days.primary_title: Day 290 · 30 Jul 2027 — Reconstruct a finite Tailwind variant API (150m)
days.practical_task: From a visual/state contract, recreate a small semantic status-badge API with complete static class maps and no copied prior component implementation.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All six supported combinations have complete static classes and visible readable labels.
- Unsupported tone is rejected; UNKNOWN uses warning and never success purely because a later record exists.
- No per-screen palette fork or dynamic class fragment remains; classes are checked against the installed Tailwind build system.

days.primary_title: Day 291 · 31 Jul 2027 — Reuse the list across two domain views (150m)
days.practical_task: Consume the same typed list composition in the Support history view and an existing owned-journey view using separate prepared domain data adapters.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Both consumers use one shared implementation and token API while preserving their distinct typed actions.
- Support cannot invoke a journey command through a generic action escape hatch; no domain fetching moves into shared UI.
- Empty/error/ready states work for both; unsupported resume remains unavailable without inventing policy or money authority.

days.primary_title: Day 292 · 01 Aug 2027 — Preserve history meaning at narrow widths (150m)
days.practical_task: Refine one responsive history-row layout to keep sequence, outcome and source action understandable at narrow widths and zoom without duplicating markup.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- At 320 px and 200% zoom, essential labels/actions remain reachable and readable without clipped controls or overlapping text.
- Visual reordering does not make keyboard or reading order misleading; sequence and outcome remain associated with the correct row.
- Long labels wrap or truncate with an accessible full-label mechanism; status is not conveyed by color alone.

days.primary_title: Day 293 · 02 Aug 2027 — Test Inter failure without losing controls (150m)
days.practical_task: Run a controlled font-load failure/delay experiment on the shared history layout and make one evidence-based fallback adjustment if needed.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All critical text and source controls are readable before Inter loads and when it never loads.
- Measure/report observed movement or clipping under matched conditions; do not invent a zero-layout-shift claim.
- Fallback preserves hierarchy and keyboard reachability; existing Inter license/asset attribution remains present and no paid font is introduced.

days.primary_title: Day 294 · 03 Aug 2027 — Announce history loading and failures clearly (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one accessible status/error communication seam for history pagination, distinguishing foreground load, background refresh and failed continuation.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Initial and user-triggered continuation outcomes have concise meaningful status text; repeated unchanged renders do not duplicate announcements.
- 503 continuation preserves existing rows and focus with an explicit Retry read action.
- 403 clears private rows and details and announces access loss; it is not a stale-data toast over exposed content.

days.primary_title: Day 295 · 04 Aug 2027 — Target invalidation after a case event (150m)
days.practical_task: Design and implement the invalidation graph for one server-confirmed existing Support event notification, refreshing only affected read keys and resetting obsolete fences.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- C1 list/summary become eligible for a deliberate fresh chain; unchanged E2 detail need not refetch under the stated contract.
- C2, V/C3 and public catalog remain untouched; duplicate notification creates no duplicate domain action.
- A notification for an old identity cannot repopulate current private state; invalidation never becomes an authorization substitute.

days.primary_title: Day 296 · 05 Aug 2027 — Diagnose a late response crossing identity (150m)
days.practical_task: Minimize a seeded frontend defect where an old Support response writes into unscoped component state after account switch, then remove the unsafe state path.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Baseline demonstrates whether old E1/E2 appear after V activates, with a precise event trace.
- Repaired sequence never renders U rows under V even when R1 ignores abort.
- Logout/switch also removes selected details and drafts; memory-only private caches remain unpersisted and no provider/write action occurs.

days.primary_title: Day 297 · 06 Aug 2027 — Integrate filter and page race handling (150m)
days.practical_task: Run and repair one cross-state interaction sequence combining a dirty filter, pending continuation and later filter replacement using the already authored components.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Final UI shows only CLOSED/E6 with its own fence; old seq 3, 4 are never appended.
- Old E2 dialog/selection closes or is explicitly reset before it can display out-of-filter stale content.
- Dirty editor clears only on Apply; no extra request loop, duplicate mutation or leaked old-scope data is introduced.

days.primary_title: Day 298 · 07 Aug 2027 — Verify shared variants in production CSS (150m)
days.practical_task: Use the actual reconciled production build to test every finite shared history/list variant and add the smallest source-detection/static-class fix if a variant is missing.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each supported variant has the intended computed style in production output, not merely a class string in the DOM.
- Focused/disabled/error states remain distinguishable with readable labels at 320 px.
- No dynamic class interpolation, dependency upgrade or per-domain duplicate CSS is used; absent build readiness is BLOCKED_NOT_READY.

days.primary_title: Day 299 · 08 Aug 2027 — Specify the bounded Support explorer seam (150m)
days.practical_task: Inspect the actual current Support public model, map only the case-history read seam and execute a learner-authored contract model for its allowed fields and assignment scope.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The mapping identifies actual supported model fields and explicitly marks missing seams BLOCKED_NOT_READY rather than inventing repository paths.
- Executable model returns C1’s four events and denies C2 without protected payload access.
- Model rejects consumer answers, raw provider payload and money authority fields; the slice remains read-only and bounded by limit 1–50.
- The executable filter/decoder contract covers the proposed history-kind registry, including UNKNOWN and SYSTEM_NOTICE; existing authoritative event types are mapped without rewriting historical business records.

days.primary_title: Day 300 · 09 Aug 2027 — Connect Support authorization to the read handler (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement the smallest reconciled Spring entry handler that binds authenticated Support scope, parsed filters and the existing history-read service without exposing caller-chosen authority.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Valid U/C1 request derives current scope from the authenticated context and returns at most 2 events.
- Caller actor/generation claims cannot grant authority; invalid request fields fail before private lookup.
- C2/C9 produce the same safe denial shape and zero decrypt/provider calls; no generic status/payment mutation route is added.

days.primary_title: Day 301 · 10 Aug 2027 — Join exact audit references into Support rows (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one repository projection join for the vertical slice that resolves allowed exact audit/source references without dropping unknown outcomes or multiplying events.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Four source events produce four rows, retaining UNKNOWN and both observations without multiplying joins.
- Sequence 1 resolves revision 2; two M3 observations still reference one effect rather than implying amountMinor=25000, currency=INR.
- Unassigned U/C2 yields no rows; no protected source payload is decrypted merely to render the list.

days.primary_title: Day 302 · 11 Aug 2027 — Wire the typed Support history hook (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement the actual API-specific TanStack hook for the reconciled Spring response, including runtime decoding before cache admission and the established key/cancellation policy.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Valid response produces the typed page and exact continuation under the correct scope key.
- Malformed revision/event kind never enters the cache as valid data and is shown as a contract failure, not empty success.
- 403 clears the private page; AbortSignal reaches the transport; no private persistence or new QueryClient per render is introduced.

days.primary_title: Day 303 · 12 Aug 2027 — Compose the Support explorer view (150m)
days.practical_task: Connect the existing filter editor, fenced-page hook and reusable list into one read-only Support case-history view with safe source-detail entry points.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- User can load page 1, move to page 2 and open an allowed exact source reference without leaving the declared scope.
- Empty, 503 and source-unavailable states remain distinct with meaningful controls and labels.
- No business-write call occurs during mount, filtering, pagination or source view; browser analytics is not authoritative history.

days.primary_title: Day 304 · 13 Aug 2027 — Recheck access when opening a history source (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement the vertical slice’s source-open action so it revalidates current case/source authorization instead of trusting an earlier list response.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Unchanged authorized scope opens only A1/revision 2, never latest revision 3.
- After revocation, no source detail or plaintext is returned and decrypt-call count is 0.
- Forged C2 reference fails identically to an unavailable private source; a cached list or UUID is never sufficient authority.

days.primary_title: Day 305 · 14 Aug 2027 — Regress cross-scope explorer entry points (150m)
days.practical_task: Author a compact adversarial test matrix for the finished explorer’s list, continuation and source-open entry points, then repair at most one missing guard.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All unauthorized paths release 0 private-canary bytes and perform 0 decrypt/provider calls.
- Unknown and forbidden resource paths share the safe outward shape; cursor possession grants no authority.
- Authorized unchanged U/C1 still returns valid pages/sources; the fix must not disable the feature or broaden queries.

days.primary_title: Day 306 · 15 Aug 2027 — Allowlist explorer responses and diagnostics (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one explicit response/log projection for the Support explorer that keeps necessary event identifiers while rejecting accidental raw entity or exception serialization.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Successful response contains only the agreed minimal fields and still resolves exact source identity.
- None of the three markers appears in response, logs, error body or analytics capture on success or failure.
- Safe outcome/request diagnostics remain usable; authorization/decrypt ordering is unchanged and reads stay functional when analytics drops.

days.primary_title: Day 307 · 16 Aug 2027 — Resume an explorer deep link after bootstrap (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one cold-refresh/deep-link transition for the finished SPA explorer using session bootstrap, server refetch and safe URL filter restoration.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Private query waits until session resolution; U gets an authorized fresh page with normalized filters.
- V/signed out shows no data flash and does not read C1 before authority is known.
- Private history, decrypted content and private query/mutation state are not persisted; refresh creates no business mutation and does not claim SSR hydration.

days.primary_title: Day 308 · 17 Aug 2027 — Clear visible details after assignment loss (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one authorization-loss state transition across the explorer list, selected row, dialog and local filter state without introducing a new polling mechanism.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- 403 clears private rows, selection, source body and private in-flight state before the access-denied render.
- Late older 200 cannot refill the view; no automatic reattempt under revoked authority occurs.
- Public catalog and benign visual preferences remain available; focus moves to a message or sign-in control with a meaningful name.

days.primary_title: Day 309 · 18 Aug 2027 — Keep explorer use independent of analytics (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement and test one best-effort analytics boundary around the existing explorer interaction, preserving the approved allowlist and proving it cannot block history use.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- History load, pagination and source view complete under telemetry failure with unchanged authoritative rows.
- If an approved event exists, retry count<=3 and queue<=20 with observable drop; without an allowlist, emit 0 events and report that state.
- No form value, raw URL, source text, amount, credential or arbitrary property enters payload; analytics never advances a journey or creates audit truth.

days.primary_title: Day 310 · 19 Aug 2027 — Measure one bounded explorer interaction (150m)
days.practical_task: Measure request/query/render work for the existing page 1-to-page 2 explorer interaction and test one narrowly justified reduction or retain the baseline.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Every valid run shows sequences 1–20 then 21–40 with no other case and no payload decrypt.
- Report actual request/query counts and timings including failures; compare only matched conditions and do not claim production capacity.
- Any change preserves page fence, authorization and keyboard behavior; absent profiling tools are recorded rather than timing numbers invented.

days.primary_title: Day 311 · 20 Aug 2027 — Add one half-open date-filter variant (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a small vertical requirement change: apply the already validated half-open UTC date range consistently from URL/filter model through the history query.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- First two events are included and Aug 2 midnight is excluded; timezone-equivalent instants normalize consistently.
- Invalid or over 31-day ranges fail before query; the old cursor cannot be used with the new range.
- Scope check, fence and exact source references remain unchanged; this read-only filter creates no audit, money or policy change.

days.primary_title: Day 312 · 21 Aug 2027 — Demonstrate the integrated explorer contract (150m)
days.practical_task: Execute one prepared end-to-end Support explorer scenario and author the specified empty-fence boundary assertion, or an equally bounded newly observed defect assertion with an explicit oracle.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- First chain shows 1–4 and not 5; Refresh starts a fence 5 chain; UNKNOWN remains visible beside the reconciled outcome.
- C2 is denied and no source plaintext is read without scope; analytics failure leaves the flow usable.
- Demonstration references one M3 effect and performs 0 money/provider commands; candidate, fixture and assistance are explicit and missing checks remain NOT_RUN.
- The learner-authored additional probe returns an empty authorized C0 page with no continuation and no source lookup; this new assertion is recorded separately from reused smoke checks.

days.primary_title: Day 313 · 22 Aug 2027 — Reproduce and challenge the frozen explorer (150m)
days.practical_task: Independently reproduce the exact local explorer candidate and author one executable negative check that detects a candidate/fixture mismatch before interpreting smoke results.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Matching run displays the four expected source-linked events under authorized U and denies V.
- Mismatch detector rejects CAND-OLD/FIX-OTHER receipts instead of accepting their PASS label.
- Mutant fixture is separately identified and produces the expected additional row after refresh; no unrun or guided result is relabeled independent.

days.primary_title: Day 314 · 23 Aug 2027 — Model consecutive observation grouping (150m)
days.practical_task: Translate an unfamiliar display-only requirement into an executable grouping model: collapse consecutive observations with the same kind, durable operation and exact source reference within one raw page.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Expected groups are [E1], [E2, E3], [E4], [E5, E6], [E7], with original IDs and first/last sequences retained.
- Changing E3 to source R1 rev 3 splits it from E2; nonconsecutive equal kinds are never merged.
- Grouping changes display only, leaves raw event count 7 and effect count 1, and never treats UNKNOWN as success.

days.primary_title: Day 315 · 24 Aug 2027 — Implement the independent grouped-row adapter (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one pure grouped-row adapter from day 86’s contract and connect it to the existing shared list without changing the server API or raw pagination.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Seven events render five groups with correct counts and expandable original order.
- Empty and singleton pages render correctly; input arrays/events are not mutated.
- Opening a source uses an original exact event reference, not a synthetic group as authority; raw continuation remains unchanged.

days.primary_title: Day 316 · 25 Aug 2027 — Attack grouped history edge cases (150m)
days.practical_task: Author adversarial tests against the independent grouping adapter and repair at most one bounded defect while preserving raw identity and authorization.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Different operation or source revision splits groups; equal kind alone never collapses records.
- Contradictory duplicate identity is rejected rather than hidden inside a group; page-local grouping does not merge fetched page boundaries.
- Revoked source-open releases no private source and makes 0 decrypt calls; grouping cannot bypass existing authority checks.

days.primary_title: Day 317 · 26 Aug 2027 — Diagnose a duplicated history row (150m)
days.practical_task: Independently diagnose an unfamiliar seeded fault that repeats a history event during a two-page explorer interaction. Build the smallest reproducer, collect discriminating evidence and identify the responsible seam without an implementation hint.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The learner reproduces the reported duplicate with the frozen fixture and records the relevant request, raw-result and rendered-event identities.
- A learner-authored discriminating probe supports one cause and rules out at least one plausible alternative; the diagnosis names a specific observed boundary rather than guessing from the symptom.
- No event/source identity is rewritten or row silently dropped to hide the symptom; assignment authorization and fence 6 remain enforced. A justified diagnosis-only result is labeled incomplete repair rather than a false pass.

days.primary_title: Day 318 · 27 Aug 2027 — Repair the diagnosed history page fault (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement the smallest repair supported by day 89’s actual diagnosis and compare the repaired grouped display with the existing ungrouped baseline on the same raw-event contract.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Both repaired grouped display and ungrouped baseline visit raw sequences 1–6 exactly once with unchanged exact source identities.
- The separately labeled one-row final page terminates without a loop or skip; sequence 7 remains excluded from the original fence-6 chain.
- The repair addresses the demonstrated cause without suppressing valid events or weakening access checks; comparison states grouping’s extra complexity without inventing a performance advantage.

days.primary_title: Day 319 · 28 Aug 2027 — Solve an unfamiliar scoped SQL mock (150m)
days.practical_task: Complete a timed independent SQL/debugging mock for an authorized case summary, then execute one new counterexample derived from the debrief within the same primary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Result is C7: (3 observations, 2 unknown, amountMinor=9000, currency=INR), C8: (0, 0, amountMinor=0, currency=INR), with no C9; historical assignments do not multiply rows.
- An extra success observation referencing M7 increments observationCount but not the confirmed sum; a fresh counterexample tests a noticed weakness.
- Record elapsed practical time, assistance and unresolved errors; total mock plus debrief remains within the day budget.

days.primary_title: Day 320 · 29 Aug 2027 — Verify the Block A mastery demonstration (150m)
days.practical_task: Run only the prepared explorer/grouping demonstration and execute a small claim-to-evidence check that rejects unsupported independent-mastery assertions for this candidate.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Prepared run visits raw 1–6 once, preserves UNKNOWN/reconciled observations, excludes 7 until refresh and denies revoked source-open before decrypt.
- Evidence gate rejects the mismatched receipt and labels guided-only work separately; claims need matching actual candidate/fixture/environment observations.
- No money/provider mutation occurs; UI keyboard/source behavior is demonstrated from the prepared component; missing or failed checks remain visible without a mastery/job guarantee.

days.primary_title: Day 321 · 30 Aug 2027 — Bound the owned-history workload (150m)
days.practical_task: Author the request-accounting and hard-stop rules for one local owned-history workload runner, then execute its ten-request dry run.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The dry run accounts for all 10 offered requests as 7 successes, 2 expected denials and 1 cancellation without omitting the cancellation.
- The runner stops at the earliest client/request/time cap, including a deliberately shortened two-second limit.
- Foreign reads return the safe denial with zero decrypt/provider calls; the measured workload changes no money or journey state.

days.primary_title: Day 322 · 31 Aug 2027 — Capture the first end-to-end latency baseline (150m)
days.practical_task: Run the prepared owned-history path and author a receipt that pairs client durations with server work and failure counts for three bounded trials.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All three trials record the same declared fixture, candidate, warmup and offered mix.
- Successful, denied, failed and cancelled responses reconcile; an injected single timeout remains visible.
- Client and server durations are labeled separately and no service-level guarantee or speedup is inferred from this local sample.

days.primary_title: Day 323 · 01 Sep 2027 — Locate a CPU-heavy history projection (150m)
days.practical_task: Capture an actual CPU recording for a synthetic repeated-formatting history projection and identify one candidate hotspot with a falsifiable call-path hypothesis.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The summary links the suspected frames to the exercised projection rather than idle/background threads.
- The reduced case returns exactly the same 20 ordered summaries as the reference fixture.
- Low sample count or missing profiler support is reported as INCONCLUSIVE or BLOCKED; authorization, decryption and business state remain unchanged.

days.primary_title: Day 324 · 02 Sep 2027 — Trace history allocation pressure (150m)
days.practical_task: Use allocation and garbage-collection observations to compare a prepared retain-all projection with its bounded-page input, without changing application behavior yet.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Record actual allocation/GC events and profiler mode for both variants, or label sampling insufficient.
- Both variants expose only the same 20 authorized summaries and no foreign rows.
- The learner distinguishes temporary allocation from retained growth and does not call absence of GC a memory-leak proof.

days.primary_title: Day 325 · 03 Sep 2027 — Measure the profiler observer effect (150m)
days.practical_task: Reconstruct the baseline measurement with recording disabled and enabled under matched conditions, then quantify the uncertainty introduced by profiling.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Three off and three on observations use identical request mix, candidate and workload bounds.
- A trial with an injected single timeout retains that failure and is not silently discarded to improve the result.
- Report observed difference and run-to-run spread without a significance or universal-overhead claim; all owner denials remain intact.

days.primary_title: Day 326 · 04 Sep 2027 — Reduce one measured projection allocation (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one bounded projection change suggested by the allocation evidence and compare it with the retained baseline using the same fixture.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All 20 returned rows, sequence order and Unknown values match the original contract.
- Empty input and a foreign-owner read remain safe and expose no protected fields.
- Record allocation events, raw timings and failures for both candidates; retain or reject the change based on evidence without inventing a speedup.

days.primary_title: Day 327 · 05 Sep 2027 — Close resources on projection failure (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement resource lifetime handling for one existing read adapter using an instrumented AutoCloseable cursor and a mapping failure.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Successful iteration closes exactly once and returns 20 rows.
- Failure on row 7 closes exactly once, returns no partial successful page and preserves the primary mapping error.
- A close failure is observable as specified by the installed language/runtime contract without logging private payloads or leaving an acquired resource active.

days.primary_title: Day 328 · 06 Sep 2027 — Separate CPU work from thread blocking (150m)
days.practical_task: Diagnose three prepared thread-state samples by capturing actual recordings while a history adapter computes, waits on a barrier or waits for a pooled permit.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Observed stacks and states distinguish runnable work, latch wait and resource acquisition, with insufficient samples labeled.
- Releasing each barrier/permit permits bounded completion; interruption cancels the waiting test without hanging.
- All worker threads terminate at the harness deadline and no diagnostic contains the encrypted payload marker.

days.primary_title: Day 329 · 07 Sep 2027 — Propagate a read deadline safely (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one deadline-aware history adapter boundary that cancels unfinished read work and preserves cleanup on timeout.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The 50 ms case returns the exact page within the test tolerance prepared for the environment.
- The 500 ms case returns the safe timeout and releases its resource; the non-cooperative case is reported as still running until observed termination.
- A late result cannot publish a page after cancellation or alter journey state, and the harness finishes within its independent safety limit.

days.primary_title: Day 330 · 08 Sep 2027 — Debug the serialized formatter incident (150m)
days.practical_task: Reproduce a disclosed shared-monitor contention mechanism and independently author a minimal experiment and one synchronization repair.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The barrier-aligned H/W probe produces observable shared-monitor waiting in the disclosed faulty variant and no corresponding monitor-blocked W in the outside-monitor control; use thread/recording evidence rather than inferring contention from latency alone.
- The reproducer separates lock-held and lock-free controls and terminates all workers.
- The repaired case preserves exact summary ordering and foreign-owner denial; before/after timings and failures are recorded without a promised gain.

days.primary_title: Day 331 · 09 Sep 2027 — Publish immutable formatting state (150m)
days.practical_task: Replace one mutable shared formatting snapshot with a safely published immutable snapshot and test a concurrent configuration swap.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Every page contains exclusively V1 or exclusively V2 labels under the defined page-snapshot contract.
- An unknown event code renders Unknown and does not mutate either shared map.
- Four-reader execution terminates without shared mutable aliasing; owner-scoped rows and financial effects are unchanged.

days.primary_title: Day 332 · 10 Sep 2027 — Reject excess projection work explicitly (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement bounded admission for the read-only projection executor and expose a safe overload result without running rejected work on the request thread.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Exactly 2 jobs run and 2 queue while the fifth receives the declared safe rejection.
- Release drains the four accepted jobs once; rejected work is never invoked later or on the caller thread.
- Shutdown leaves no queued task or retained private result, and no business-state retry is inferred from read overload.

days.primary_title: Day 333 · 11 Sep 2027 — Bound per-request parallel history reads (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one composite read that shares a deadline across two independent safe projections and cancels its sibling after a required branch fails.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Normal completion combines the correct 20 summaries and total 50 with no more than 2 active workers.
- Count failure cancels or explicitly observes termination of the summary branch and returns no misleading complete result.
- The total deadline is not restarted for the second branch; all branches release resources and unauthorized requests launch neither branch.

days.primary_title: Day 334 · 12 Sep 2027 — Verify read shutdown without leaked tasks (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement graceful shutdown for the bounded read executor and observe accepted, queued and newly rejected work at the shutdown boundary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- r5 is rejected after shutdown starts and cannot execute.
- Each of r1–r4 has one terminal completion/cancellation disposition; queued tasks are not silently lost from accounting.
- After the drain or forced-cancellation path all controlled workers terminate, private results are released and no success is claimed while a non-cooperative task remains alive.

days.primary_title: Day 335 · 13 Sep 2027 — Strengthen cancellation lifetime regressions (150m)
days.practical_task: Author a focused regression matrix that combines deadline expiry, queue rejection and close failure for the existing read adapter.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Every acquired cursor closes exactly once and rejected-before-acquire work has acquire=close=0.
- No timeout/mapping failure is presented as a complete page; the primary and suppressed errors match the contract.
- All four cases terminate within the prepared one-second safety boundary, expose no private payload and preserve the operation/journey baseline.

days.primary_title: Day 336 · 14 Sep 2027 — Defend the retained JVM change (150m)
days.practical_task: Rerun only the selected projection change against its baseline and execute a counterexample that challenges the explanation for the observed result.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Record raw timings, allocation observations and failures for both candidates under the same limits.
- The counterexample demonstrates the condition under which the hypothesized benefit disappears or honestly fails to do so.
- Exact page semantics, authorization, cleanup and queue bounds pass before any performance result is accepted; uncertain results remain labeled.

days.primary_title: Day 337 · 15 Sep 2027 — Correlate pool waits with request latency (150m)
days.practical_task: Instrument one existing history read boundary to correlate acquisition wait, query duration and request duration using safe request labels.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each request has acquisition and query observations or an explicit acquisition failure, not fabricated zero durations.
- The 2-connection limit is visible and releasing the query barrier allows waiting requests to finish.
- Metrics/logs contain no journey UUID, SQL parameter value or protected payload marker, and the owner predicate remains enforced.

days.primary_title: Day 338 · 16 Sep 2027 — Bound connection acquisition failure (150m)
days.practical_task: Configure and test one existing pool acquisition timeout within the request deadline, preserving cleanup and safe failure handling.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The third request fails with the declared safe resource-unavailable response rather than waiting indefinitely.
- After release a new owned query succeeds and pool active count returns to baseline.
- Timeout neither retries a write nor leaks private SQL details; foreign-owner requests still avoid protected-data access.

days.primary_title: Day 339 · 17 Sep 2027 — Explain skewed history query estimates (150m)
days.practical_task: Run actual query plans for one active-history predicate under the skewed fixture and compare estimated versus actual cardinality before changing an index.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Identify the largest relevant estimate/actual mismatch from captured plans, or state that estimates align.
- All result pages retain deterministic order and ownership filtering for empty/inactive/foreign cases.
- The decision distinguishes cardinality, plan shape and elapsed time; no new index or speedup is required to pass.

days.primary_title: Day 340 · 18 Sep 2027 — Remove one history N-plus-one read (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one bounded history projection that avoids per-row metadata fetches while preserving optional metadata and page cardinality.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- A 20-row page performs the declared bounded query count, at most 2, independent of whether 1 or 20 rows are returned.
- Missing source labels remain explicit Unknown and duplicate metadata cannot multiply the page rows.
- Ownership filtering occurs before result serialization; no private entity graph or encrypted payload is fetched to solve the query count.

days.primary_title: Day 341 · 19 Sep 2027 — Debug a leaked transaction connection (150m)
days.practical_task: Diagnose a seeded read-adapter failure that leaves a transaction resource held, and repair only its transaction/lifetime boundary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Before launching R3 in the faulty run, observe two checked-out connections and two retained database transactions after R1/R2 error responses; R3 reaches its configured acquisition timeout because no pool slot is free, not merely because another request happened to be slow.
- In the control/repaired run, R1 and R2 both roll back and release their connections before R3 starts; checked-out count returns to zero and R3 completes the correct 20-row owned page without an acquisition timeout. Record actual waits and the prepared environment tolerance.
- Both failing reads return safe failures rather than partial successful pages; database domain/audit/journey data remain unchanged and errors exclude raw query values. The independent 2-second cleanup releases every faulty session even if diagnosis or repair is incomplete.

days.primary_title: Day 342 · 20 Sep 2027 — Shorten a mock-operation transaction (150m)
days.practical_task: Move one prepared slow mock-provider wait outside the existing SQL transaction while preserving durable intent and atomic result recording.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Pending intent commits before the mock call and no SQL transaction remains open during the 300 ms provider wait.
- Result-recording failure rolls back result/audit/journey together and preserves the durable pending reference for reconciliation.
- No second mock acceptance or money effect occurs on the tested retry, and B cannot initiate or inspect A operation.

days.primary_title: Day 343 · 21 Sep 2027 — Reproduce the dispatch-cancel lock cycle (150m)
days.practical_task: Create a deterministic two-session reproducer for a supplied opposite lock order in dispatch and cancellation, and classify the database outcome.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The schedule observes the competing lock order and records a real deadlock victim or bounded timeout with the correct classification.
- The aborted transaction leaves no partial audit/journey/domain changes.
- After cleanup both sessions release locks; dispatch and cancellation cannot both claim incompatible success.

days.primary_title: Day 344 · 22 Sep 2027 — Enforce one dispatch-cancel lock order (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a consistent lock order for the two existing competing commands and verify both interleavings against the same fixture.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each run produces one legal winner and a safe conflict/reconciliation disposition for the loser.
- No captured schedule contains the opposite-order wait cycle; absent deadlocks are reported only for these bounded runs.
- Domain state, required audit and journey events remain atomic and no duplicate external effect is introduced.

days.primary_title: Day 345 · 23 Sep 2027 — Bound retries after serialization failure (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a bounded whole-transaction retry for one pure database claim path while keeping external calls outside the retried transaction.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Retryable failure then success opens a fresh transaction and produces exactly one committed claim.
- Three retryable failures terminate after 3 total attempts; validation/ownership failures are never retried.
- External provider call count remains zero within the retried seam and partial audit/journey writes never survive aborted attempts.

days.primary_title: Day 346 · 24 Sep 2027 — Reconstruct the bounded history query (150m)
days.practical_task: Rebuild the owner-scoped fenced history query from its contract without viewing the previous implementation, then execute adversarial cursor cases.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Pages are 6/5, 4/3 and 2/1, and appended 7 appears only on a fresh fence.
- Foreign-owner and changed-filter cursors reject safely and cannot reveal row existence through payload contents.
- Each page has at most 2 distinct rows and a captured plan supports the bounded retrieval claim without requiring a redundant index.

days.primary_title: Day 347 · 25 Sep 2027 — Observe long-transaction snapshot behavior (150m)
days.practical_task: Run a two-session read/update experiment to explain an existing history view snapshot under the installed PostgreSQL isolation level.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Record actual counts for both isolation variants and explain them against the installed server contract.
- An uncommitted W append is never presented as committed history to R.
- Rollback removes the uncommitted append/audit/journey change together, sessions close, and B remains denied.

days.primary_title: Day 348 · 26 Sep 2027 — Cancel one slow query without poisoning the pool (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement and test statement cancellation for one owned read while observing transaction cleanup and subsequent connection reuse.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The slow query receives a controlled failure and observed server work terminates or remains honestly labeled pending until safety release.
- Any failed transaction is rolled back before the connection returns to the pool; the subsequent query succeeds.
- No partial success page or automatic business-write retry is emitted, and private query parameters are absent from logs.

days.primary_title: Day 349 · 27 Sep 2027 — Test admission before database overload (150m)
