days.practical_task: Connect the existing bounded request-admission seam to pool availability for one read endpoint and measure deliberate rejection versus acquisition waiting.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- At most 2 reads hold connections and 2 wait in the application queue; the other 2 get the declared safe overload result.
- Each batch accounts for all 6 jobs and returns active/queued counts to zero after release.
- Rejected work neither acquires a connection later nor mutates state, and normal reads recover without restarting the application.

days.primary_title: Day 350 · 28 Sep 2027 — Inspect index cost without chasing a speedup (150m)
days.practical_task: Compare one existing index with one instructor-prepared candidate index on the same history filter, including a bounded append workload.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Both candidates return the same deterministic authorized page, including empty and inactive filters.
- Record actual index size, plan shape, query durations and append observations rather than asserting a gain.
- Appends preserve event uniqueness and atomic audit/journey writes; comparison occurs only in disposable copies with cleanup verified.

days.primary_title: Day 351 · 29 Sep 2027 — Measure pool size against the same workload (150m)
days.practical_task: Run a matched two-setting pool experiment and interpret queueing, failures and database work instead of selecting the largest throughput number.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each setting records active/acquiring connections, raw latencies, achieved rate, failures and the same injected delay.
- No trial exceeds the database/session/load envelope and all held resources recover after the delay.
- Select or decline a configuration change with stated uncertainty; no owner/atomicity invariant may be traded for a better timing.

days.primary_title: Day 352 · 30 Sep 2027 — Diagnose a cross-layer saturation variant (150m)
days.practical_task: Identify whether an unfamiliar slow owned-history run is dominated by allocation, acquisition wait or a locked query, and execute one discriminating counterexperiment.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Use at least two corroborating sources, such as thread stacks and pool/database waits, to support the chosen cause.
- The counterexperiment removes or isolates only that mechanism and records actual changed or unchanged observations.
- All 12 requests and resources are accounted for; the diagnostic never bypasses ownership or changes business effects.

days.primary_title: Day 353 · 01 Oct 2027 — Carry a deadline through mock dispatch (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one operation deadline propagated through admission, database claim and mock-provider invocation, with an explicit unknown-result disposition.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The provider receives only the remaining budget and later stages never restart the original 500 ms budget.
- A timeout after possible acceptance preserves o1/p1 or its reconciliation reference as unknown, never a definitive failure or a new operation.
- B is rejected before provider/decrypt access; authoritative state/audit/journey recording is atomic.

days.primary_title: Day 354 · 02 Oct 2027 — Classify retryable dispatch outcomes (150m)
days.practical_task: Author the retry decision for one existing mock dispatch adapter and test known rejection, transport uncertainty and invalid input separately.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Only the explicitly safe temporary rejection is eligible for another attempt under the same o1 identity.
- Unknown acceptance routes to reconciliation without a fresh dispatch; validation and ownership failures are never retried.
- Duplicate p1 creates no second dispatch/audit-derived money effect and cannot advance the journey twice.

days.primary_title: Day 355 · 03 Oct 2027 — Bound retry backoff and exhaustion (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a deadline-aware backoff schedule for safe retryable dispatch failures and verify it with a fake clock plus one bounded real-timer observation.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The model schedules no more than 3 total attempts and never starts an attempt after the remaining deadline is exhausted.
- Known permanent failure and unknown result bypass retry even when a retry slot remains.
- The real run records actual delays and scheduler tolerance separately from modeled values; all attempts retain o1 and no duplicate business effect.

days.primary_title: Day 356 · 04 Oct 2027 — Cap the durable pending-work backlog (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one transactional admission rule for pending dispatch work so a full bounded queue rejects new work without losing already committed intent.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Before a slot opens, admission reports the declared safe capacity result and adds no partial operation/audit/journey record.
- After one completion, at most one of the two competing new operations is admitted and pending count never exceeds 4 under the specified schedule.
- Existing pending identities survive rejected admissions; no new runtime broker or process-only queue is substituted for durability.

days.primary_title: Day 357 · 05 Oct 2027 — Strengthen durable identity replay regressions (150m)
days.practical_task: Write new regression tests for operation replay after response-cache expiry and for changed accepted input under a reused idempotency key.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Expired transport cache does not permit a second dispatch or money effect for o1.
- Changed amount or revision under the same idempotency key conflicts and never silently accepts the new tuple.
- Exact replay preserves the confirmed reference and existing event relationships; B cannot replay A operation.

days.primary_title: Day 358 · 06 Oct 2027 — Commit one outbox intent atomically (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement the existing operation-to-outbox seam in the owning transaction and fault it after each write boundary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- A successful transaction exposes one durable work item with matching operation/audit/journey references.
- Every injected pre-commit failure leaves all four structures at the before-state.
- A retry under o1 produces at most one work item and no provider invocation inside the transaction.

days.primary_title: Day 359 · 07 Oct 2027 — Claim pending work across two workers (150m)
days.practical_task: Author one database-backed batch-claim query and validate concurrent workers with deterministic barriers.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each worker receives at most 2 distinct items and no item belongs to both active claim sets.
- A held row does not cause unbounded blocking; record the actual installed locking behavior and remaining unclaimed item.
- Rollback releases the uncommitted claim without losing durable intent; provider calls remain outside claim transactions.

days.primary_title: Day 360 · 08 Oct 2027 — Fence stale worker completion (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one completion guard that checks the current durable claim token before committing a dispatch result.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Token 7 cannot commit a domain/audit/journey completion once token 8 owns the claim.
- The late p1 observation is handled by the defined safe reconciliation path and does not authorize a fresh external effect.
- A valid token-8 definitive result commits once with atomic references; changed payload under o1 still conflicts.

days.primary_title: Day 361 · 09 Oct 2027 — Observe pending work after process restart (150m)
days.practical_task: Run an actual controlled application-worker stop/restart between committed intent and mock invocation, then verify the pending item is still claimable.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The process identities show a real worker restart and o1 remains present in the unchanged database.
- One claim cycle processes the existing identity rather than creating a new intent; mock acceptance occurs at most once in this schedule.
- A second restart does not duplicate the confirmed effect; no cross-process encrypted-data recovery claim is made from this pending-work test.

days.primary_title: Day 362 · 10 Oct 2027 — Rehearse disclosed lost-response recovery (150m)
days.practical_task: Execute a mechanism-disclosed guided recovery drill: the instructor states that the mock provider accepts p1 and the worker stops before local definitive SQL commit. Reproduce the resulting uncertainty, classify the surviving facts and author a no-blind-redelivery guard for the existing reconciliation path. This drill does not assess independent unfamiliar diagnosis.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Database retains pending/unknown o1 while simulator evidence shows p1; missing local success is not labeled provider failure.
- The learner-authored guard prevents blind resubmission and routes to reconciliation under the same durable identity.
- Result/audit/journey state is internally atomic and no second money/dispatch effect appears after restart.
- The receipt explicitly labels the fault mechanism as disclosed and recovery work as guided. It separates learner-authored implementation/test evidence from unfamiliar-diagnosis evidence; this run is not counted as an independent unfamiliar diagnosis.

days.primary_title: Day 363 · 11 Oct 2027 — Reconcile one unknown dispatch outcome (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one existing reconciliation seam that consumes a mock observation for o1 and records a definitive result only when evidence supports it.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Confirmed p1 commits the matching allowed state plus audit/journey once; duplicate lookup does not repeat advancement.
- Still unknown preserves uncertainty and schedules only bounded re-observation, never a new business effect.
- Recording failure rolls back state/audit/journey together while the original durable reference remains usable; B remains unauthorized.

days.primary_title: Day 364 · 12 Oct 2027 — Isolate mock dispatch from history reads (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one bulkhead between mock-provider work and local owned-history reads, then observe recovery after provider tasks stall.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Third mock job receives the defined capacity result while accepted durable work remains accounted for.
- History requests retain their own bounded resources and complete or report observed failure without waiting on the provider bulkhead.
- After release no permit/task leaks remain and unknown accepted operations still reconcile under their original identities.

days.primary_title: Day 365 · 13 Oct 2027 — Drain a durable worker during shutdown (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one shutdown sequence that stops new claims, bounds in-flight waiting and leaves unresolved operations durably recoverable.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- No new work is claimed after shutdown begins and w3 stays durable pending.
- w2 is retained as unresolved with its operation reference rather than falsely failed or blindly replayed.
- After restart the prepared reconcile path resolves w2 at most once; w1 is not repeated and all authoritative writes remain atomic.

days.primary_title: Day 366 · 14 Oct 2027 — Expire stale work without erasing intent (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one ready-work selection rule that distinguishes request deadline expiry from durable operation recovery obligations.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- w1 follows the reviewed expired-before-dispatch disposition without invoking the mock provider.
- w2 remains eligible for safe reconciliation despite caller timeout; w3 is not claimed early.
- No expiry deletes required operation/audit/journey references or invents a cancellation/refund effect; model timing and actual durability are labeled separately.

days.primary_title: Day 367 · 15 Oct 2027 — Reconstruct a fenced work claimant (150m)
days.practical_task: Rebuild the bounded claim-and-complete seam from the public operation contract with the previous implementation hidden.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- No two active claims own the same item/token and each batch contains at most 1 item.
- Rolled-back claim leaves its item claimable; stale token 11 cannot complete token-12 work.
- Completion commits domain/audit/journey once under the existing durable identity and never sends a provider call inside SQL.

days.primary_title: Day 368 · 16 Oct 2027 — Verify bounded recovery under mixed faults (150m)
days.practical_task: Execute one prepared durable-operation scenario combining overload and a lost response, then independently justify the terminal dispositions.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- o1 has one confirmed effect despite safe retries and o2 reaches confirmed only through reconciliation.
- o3 rejection adds no partial intent and later explicit admission uses its original approved inputs.
- All attempts are bounded and accounted for; domain/audit/journey relationships and immutable money totals remain unchanged except the permitted confirmed transitions.

days.primary_title: Day 369 · 17 Oct 2027 — Validate local configuration before startup (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement validation for one existing local operating configuration boundary and expose a safe configuration fingerprint.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Valid configuration starts the pinned local candidate and reports a nonsecret version/fingerprint.
- Every invalid variant fails before accepting work with a safe field-level error.
- No password/key/connection credential is printed, and configuration validation creates no new account, credential or access grant.

days.primary_title: Day 370 · 18 Oct 2027 — Separate readiness from process liveness (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one health/readiness boundary that distinguishes a running process from its ability to perform the required database-backed operation.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Process liveness remains truthful while readiness reports the required dependency unavailable.
- Restored dependency leads to observed readiness recovery without exposing database details in the public response.
- A health request cannot mutate business data or decrypt the protected marker and never hangs past its bounded probe policy.

days.primary_title: Day 371 · 19 Oct 2027 — Verify local start-stop process identity (150m)
days.practical_task: Author and execute one local start/stop wrapper using only reconciled existing controls, checking actual process identity and listening socket ownership.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Normal start identifies the actual candidate process and its expected local listener; stop removes that listener.
- Occupied-port start fails safely and does not terminate the unrelated fixture process.
- A second stop is safe and leaves no worker tasks; no global process kill, firewall, port exposure or security setting is changed.

days.primary_title: Day 372 · 20 Oct 2027 — Correlate a local incident with safe logs (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one structured incident log event linking request, operation and fault category through safe opaque diagnostic references.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each case yields the declared safe event category and correlation reference sufficient to follow that local incident.
- PRIVATE-MARKER-42, raw SQL parameters, credentials and full object/consumer payloads are absent from logs and error responses.
- Logs do not substitute for required transaction audit and a failed audit transaction cannot be claimed durable from a log line.

days.primary_title: Day 373 · 21 Oct 2027 — Strengthen log-redaction failure regressions (150m)
days.practical_task: Author a regression suite that forces validation, timeout and nested-exception paths through the existing logging boundary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Neither marker appears in application logs, safe errors or diagnostic receipts across all three paths.
- Useful safe error categories and request references survive redaction; the test is not passed by suppressing every event.
- Owner denial occurs before decrypt; rejected logging input cannot change authoritative audit/journey state.

days.primary_title: Day 374 · 22 Oct 2027 — Gate a local release on a failing invariant (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one existing CI/local build gate that blocks candidate publication when the owned-history authorization regression fails.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- C1 failure produces a nonzero gate result and no eligible release artifact marker.
- C0 produces the matching successful test/artifact manifest with candidate identity.
- Skipping or swallowing the failed test cannot produce an eligible artifact; logs contain no protected values and no remote deployment occurs.

days.primary_title: Day 375 · 23 Oct 2027 — Reproduce one local build artifact (150m)
days.practical_task: Run the existing build twice from the same locked candidate and diagnose one prepared environment-dependent difference in its artifact manifest.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Record source, toolchain and dependency identifiers for both builds before comparing checksums and required assets.
- Detect the prepared timestamp or missing-asset difference and distinguish byte equality from functional completeness.
- A required-asset mismatch fails release eligibility; an explained nondeterministic field is not mislabeled byte-reproducible.

days.primary_title: Day 376 · 24 Oct 2027 — Test an expand-only schema release (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one backward-compatible additive schema seam for a nullable safe diagnostic label and run old/new candidate compatibility checks.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- C0 can read new rows without depending on the added field and C1 handles old rows with the field absent.
- Failed migration execution rolls back cleanly or reports the actual tool behavior without assuming transactional DDL support beyond the installed flow.
- Existing money, composite revision, audit/journey and encrypted envelope relationships are unchanged; no private field is duplicated into the label.

days.primary_title: Day 377 · 25 Oct 2027 — Roll back the local application candidate (150m)
days.practical_task: Execute and verify one local application rollback from C1 to C0 against the expanded schema while retaining newly written compatible data.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The running process/artifact identity after rollback is the retained C0 candidate, not just the requested version string.
- C0 reads both original and newly written compatible records and B remains denied before decrypt.
- No money/audit/journey record is deleted or rewritten to make rollback pass; incompatible rollback is reported BLOCKED rather than applying a destructive workaround.

days.primary_title: Day 378 · 26 Oct 2027 — Diagnose the disposable database route (150m)
days.practical_task: Diagnose one prepared local application-to-database connectivity failure using process, listener and existing container/network observations.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Evidence distinguishes no listener, wrong target and authentication failure without exposing credentials.
- Correcting the supplied nonsecret target or using authorized existing start controls restores the bounded owned-read probe.
- No firewall, VPN, persistent grant, public port or unrelated container is changed; failed probes terminate within configured timeouts.

days.primary_title: Day 379 · 27 Oct 2027 — Debug a mismatched restore manifest (150m)
days.practical_task: Diagnose one intentionally mismatched archive/schema manifest and execute the restore preflight guard in a disposable target without decrypting data.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The guard compares actual archive/schema/count evidence and detects the selected mismatch.
- Incompatible or inconsistent input is rejected before replacing target data or claiming recovered content.
- The original retained archive stays unchanged and no decrypt/key access occurs during this metadata-only diagnostic.

days.primary_title: Day 380 · 28 Oct 2027 — Capture a consistent encrypted-data backup (150m)
days.practical_task: Execute one approved disposable-database backup and validate its actual manifest and authoritative record relationships while writes are controlled.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The captured backup represents one documented consistent point with exact counts and referenced business identities.
- An altered copy fails integrity/manifest checks while the retained original remains usable.
- Protected payload columns retain envelopes; field encryption is not mislabeled full-backup or host-volume encryption, and no key/plaintext marker enters the archive receipt.

days.primary_title: Day 381 · 29 Oct 2027 — Verify retained teaching-key readiness (150m)
days.practical_task: Exercise the existing approved teaching-key resolver before and after a controlled application process restart using one authorized encrypted canary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- A resolves the same declared retained teaching-key version after actual process restart and recovers exact canary bytes only if that mechanism exists.
- B is denied before resolver/decrypt calls; logs and receipts contain neither key material nor canary plaintext.
- With only an ephemeral key or missing approval/mechanism, report BLOCKED_NOT_READY/KEY_UNAVAILABLE and no successful cross-process recovery; execute the supplied negative resolver test only.

days.primary_title: Day 382 · 30 Oct 2027 — Restore one authorized encrypted snapshot (150m)
days.practical_task: Restore the retained bounded archive into an approved disposable target and verify recovered relationships and authorized content through the actual application.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Recovered A content matches the snapshot through the authorized adapter after a real process boundary.
- B is denied before decrypt and tampered envelope copy fails closed; no key or plaintext marker enters logs.
- The 120000 minor-unit effect, audit reference and ordered journey relationships match exactly; missing keys/schema/data produce BLOCKED or FAIL rather than an empty successful restore.

days.primary_title: Day 383 · 31 Oct 2027 — Fail recovery closed when the key is unavailable (150m)
days.practical_task: Execute the prepared key-unavailable recovery mode and implement one guard against plaintext fallback or misleading empty-success behavior.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Unavailable key returns KEY_UNAVAILABLE and preserves the encrypted records for later recovery.
- No empty payload, plaintext fallback or successful readiness/restore claim is emitted.
- Restoring the approved resolver mode allows the original authorized canary check only if day 153 key proof remains valid; B stays denied and no key material is logged.

days.primary_title: Day 384 · 01 Nov 2027 — Reconstruct the local startup guard (150m)
days.practical_task: Rebuild the safe startup preflight from the operating contract with the earlier wrapper hidden, then run valid, occupied-port and incompatible-schema cases.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Only the valid case accepts work and identifies the actual candidate/process.
- Port conflict leaves the unrelated process alive and schema incompatibility leaves data unchanged.
- No credentials, security settings or hidden catch-up setup are introduced; every rejection has a safe diagnostic and nonzero outcome.

days.primary_title: Day 385 · 02 Nov 2027 — Test retention without breaking audit links (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one bounded local retention eligibility query for synthetic telemetry while protecting authoritative transaction and journey references.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Only day-1 analytics and the unheld eligible draft enter the reviewed deletion set; day-39 analytics and held records do not.
- Required audit, immutable money effects and referenced retained recovery data remain intact under the supplied contract.
- Dry run changes no rows and execution on the disposable fixture matches the reviewed set; teaching windows are not presented as legal retention policy.

days.primary_title: Day 386 · 03 Nov 2027 — Rehearse one local recovery runbook (150m)
days.practical_task: Follow the reconstructed operating controls to recover one stopped disposable database dependency and verify the candidate rather than rehearsing every incident at once.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Identify the actual stopped dependency from process/listener evidence and use only its authorized start control.
- Readiness recovers, A sees the expected snapshot and B is denied before decrypt; counts/effects match the original manifest.
- Record recovery elapsed time and actual actions without calling this backup restore, high availability or production disaster recovery.

days.primary_title: Day 387 · 04 Nov 2027 — Capture the history-view browser baseline (150m)
days.practical_task: Record one production-build history-view interaction and correlate render commits, local requests and visible completion under the fixed browser fixture.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Three bounded traces preserve the same candidate, fixture, viewport and interaction ordering.
- Record actual commits, request durations, visible completion and errors; missing timing APIs or noisy samples are labeled.
- Final content matches the authoritative filtered page, has no B/A leakage and remains keyboard operable with explicit loading/failure states.

days.primary_title: Day 388 · 05 Nov 2027 — Stabilize semantic history query identity (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one owner-scoped query-key/options factory that excludes incidental render state while retaining every server-result-changing filter.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Five renders with equal semantic inputs reuse one logical query subject to the frozen freshness policy.
- Status, cursor and account changes produce distinct permitted identities; removing the owner dimension fails the regression.
- No private query is persisted or shared across accounts; late A response after switch is discarded.

days.primary_title: Day 389 · 06 Nov 2027 — Memoize only the measured history seam (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one targeted rendering optimization for the measured summary-row or derivation seam and compare matched traces.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Unchanged rows avoid only the work justified by actual profiler observations, or the proposed optimization is rejected.
- The changed label becomes visible immediately under the defined state contract; no stale closure or omitted dependency hides it.
- Keyboard/focus and owner-cache behavior match baseline; record raw timing spread and failures rather than promised savings.

days.primary_title: Day 390 · 07 Nov 2027 — Cancel stale history filter responses (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one query cancellation/late-result guard for rapid filter changes while maintaining an accessible truthful loading state.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Confirmed results remain visible after the late pending response; abort-ignoring adapters cannot publish stale data.
- Account switch removes A data and neither late response recreates it in the private cache.
- Loading/error announcements and keyboard focus remain usable; cancellation does not trigger a mutation or unbounded retry.

days.primary_title: Day 391 · 08 Nov 2027 — Keep local filter typing responsive (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one measured local expensive-label preview boundary so input state stays immediate while the derived preview may lag explicitly.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Typed characters remain in the input in order, including deletion to empty, while any deferred preview is visibly identified.
- Apply uses the current typed value exactly and issues the intended owner-scoped request once.
- No unapproved debounce changes the authoritative filter semantics; recorded responsiveness may remain inconclusive and keyboard/status behavior stays accessible.

days.primary_title: Day 392 · 09 Nov 2027 — Share one history fetch across compositions (150m)
days.practical_task: Reuse the same typed query options across the page and its safe summary composition, then test request deduplication and failure recovery.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Equivalent simultaneous consumers share one in-flight query under the declared installed TanStack behavior.
- A failed request yields truthful error state in both consumers and the explicit retry does not create an uncontrolled duplicate burst.
- Different owner/filter results remain separate and account cleanup removes both consumers private data.

days.primary_title: Day 393 · 10 Nov 2027 — Strengthen fast-path accessibility regressions (150m)
days.practical_task: Author regression tests for focus, announcements and narrow-layout behavior after the selected rendering and fetch changes.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Focus stays on a meaningful control after result replacement and returns correctly after the error retry.
- Loading, empty and error outcomes are perceivable without color alone; no duplicate noisy status announcement is introduced.
- Long text and zoom preserve content/control access without private data leakage or suppressing required content to improve timing.

days.primary_title: Day 394 · 11 Nov 2027 — Split one optional history panel safely (150m)
days.practical_task: Add one lazy-loading boundary around a nonessential safe history explanation panel and verify chunk failure recovery.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Core history and owned resume remain usable before the optional panel is requested.
- Opening the panel fetches the expected actual chunk and presents an accessible fallback; chunk failure produces a retryable error without blanking the page.
- Production asset measurements and new request cost are recorded; no assumed byte reduction or private data persistence is claimed.

days.primary_title: Day 395 · 12 Nov 2027 — Verify production styles after splitting (150m)
days.practical_task: Validate one finite Tailwind variant set in the production build after the panel split and repair a prepared missing-style boundary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All four states render their intended semantic distinction in the actual production build.
- Unknown/error remain understandable without color and with system-font fallback at the narrow viewport.
- The fix does not safelist arbitrary user input or introduce raw HTML; asset sizes are observed and no entire styling-system rewrite occurs.

days.primary_title: Day 396 · 13 Nov 2027 — Observe private cache disposal on account switch (150m)
days.practical_task: Measure and test one private query-cache lifecycle boundary during repeated navigation and account changes.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- After each logout, A-owned private query keys and in-flight publish rights are absent.
- B content never includes any A summary even if a delayed A response completes during a cycle.
- No private record enters browser storage; heap observations include tool/GC limits and are not called a memory-leak diagnosis without corroborating retention evidence.

days.primary_title: Day 397 · 14 Nov 2027 — Specify a public projection reuse experiment (150m)
days.practical_task: Author and execute the contract for a removable in-process public-catalog projection alternative to repeated derivation, using an executable counterexample before implementation.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Reference output preserves source version, category and Unknown semantics for all 100 public plans.
- Passing private data or an owner-scoped response rejects at the boundary rather than entering shared memory.
- A V1→V2 counterexample demonstrates why version identity is required; acceptance criteria include raw measurements and permit retaining the uncached baseline.

days.primary_title: Day 398 · 15 Nov 2027 — Implement removable public projection reuse (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one bounded in-process public derivation cache behind the existing projection interface with the reference implementation preserved.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Every result is exactly equivalent to the reference for that source/version/category including Unknown values.
- At most 2 entries are retained and an evicted key recomputes correctly.
- Private or malformed input is rejected, no consumer data is persisted and disabling the adapter returns to the original implementation.

days.primary_title: Day 399 · 16 Nov 2027 — Coalesce concurrent public derivations (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one per-key single-flight seam for the bounded public projection adapter and test concurrent failure cleanup.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The 4 equal-key callers invoke the derivation once and receive equivalent immutable results on success.
- A failed derivation completes all waiters safely, removes failed in-flight state and permits the later bounded retry.
- Different category/version keys do not alias and no user-private key or result enters the shared structure.

days.primary_title: Day 400 · 17 Nov 2027 — Measure public reuse against recomputation (150m)
days.practical_task: Run the retained public reference and optional adapter under matched local request mixes, measuring both hit-heavy and version-churn cases.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All four candidate/mix combinations record raw durations, completed/failed counts, derivation calls and retained entry counts.
- The churn workload cannot exceed the 2-entry bound or return a wrong-version projection.
- Report actual gains, regressions or inconclusive results and preserve the simpler baseline when benefits do not justify complexity; no extrapolated scale claim.

days.primary_title: Day 401 · 18 Nov 2027 — Invalidate a changed public source safely (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one version-change publication boundary and prove a reader cannot receive a V1 projection labeled V2.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each result content matches its declared source version and V1 completion never overwrites the V2 entry.
- Unknown or unavailable V2 fails explicitly instead of relabeling a stale V1 result as current.
- No cached public fact is converted into eligibility, coverage or a payable quote; private API responses remain outside the cache.

days.primary_title: Day 402 · 19 Nov 2027 — Challenge service extraction with a fault model (150m)
days.practical_task: Build and execute one small counterexample model comparing the retained in-process projection boundary with a hypothetical extracted boundary.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Both models preserve the same public version/Unknown output contract on successful requests.
- The extracted model accounts for timeout, retry and partial availability explicitly rather than treating the network as a free local call.
- Separate modeled costs from day 172 physical observations and state what new evidence would be needed before authorizing any runtime service or dependency.

days.primary_title: Day 403 · 20 Nov 2027 — Roll back public reuse without stale results (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement and execute one existing local configuration switch back to the reference public projection while requests are in flight.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- After the switch, new requests use the reference implementation and return exact V2 content.
- Late cached work cannot republish itself as the active implementation or relabel V1 results.
- Shared adapter entries/in-flight state are drained or safely abandoned within the prepared bound; no private cache behavior or production setting is changed.

days.primary_title: Day 404 · 21 Nov 2027 — Defend the measured architecture decision (150m)
days.practical_task: Execute one final counterexample against the selected public projection implementation and defend retaining or removing the optional adapter.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The selected implementation handles eviction and failure without wrong-version results or unbounded work.
- The decision names actual day 172 observations and separately labels assumptions from day 174.
- Reference rollback still passes and private-cache, source/Unknown and accessibility constraints remain intact; rejecting the optimization is a valid outcome.

days.primary_title: Day 405 · 22 Nov 2027 — Reproduce the Block B operating candidate (150m)
days.practical_task: Independently reproduce the frozen local candidate and execute the separate OPS-SNAPSHOT integrity smoke and FRONT-HISTORY browser smoke, investigating only the first concrete mismatch. Keep fixture-lane identities explicit; do not treat their different counts as one integrated snapshot.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Observed process, build, schema and fixture-target identities match the frozen manifest for each named lane; a swapped or missing lane label fails verification rather than being relabeled after observing counts.
- OPS-SNAPSHOT SQL smoke confirms one journey per owner, A event count 2, B event count 0, one immutable capture effect totaling 120000 INR minor units and its existing audit relationship. The read-only smoke leaves all snapshot rows unchanged and does not claim this lane contains the 120/10 frontend summaries.
- FRONT-HISTORY browser smoke renders 20 of A 120 summaries on the first page, 10 of B 10 on B own page, and safely denies B requesting A history with zero unauthorized decrypt/provider calls. No late A result repopulates B private cache.
- Every observation and claim identifies its lane and actual candidate. Passing either smoke cannot establish the other lane result or one integrated snapshot; absent prerequisites are BLOCKED_NOT_READY and no physical restore or durable-worker result is inferred.

days.primary_title: Day 406 · 23 Nov 2027 — Specify an unfamiliar claim-priority rule (150m)
days.practical_task: Translate an unfamiliar bounded worker-priority requirement into an executable contract and challenge it with a starvation counterexample.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- First batch selects one urgent item and n1; neither future n2 nor two urgent items can occupy that batch.
- With no ready normal, a batch may take up to 2 ready urgent items under the written rule; ties are stable.
- Selection never authorizes a foreign operation, bypasses a claim token or changes business-effect identity; starvation limits are stated rather than universally claimed.

days.primary_title: Day 407 · 24 Nov 2027 — Implement the priority claimant independently (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement only the priority-selection seam specified on day 178 against the existing real database claim interface.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each worker obeys the per-batch priority rule for the ready unclaimed rows visible under the reviewed contract.
- No operation is claimed by both workers; future n2 is excluded and deterministic tie behavior is recorded.
- Rollback leaves work eligible for a later claim, provider calls stay outside SQL and original operation/accepted tuple identity is preserved.

days.primary_title: Day 408 · 25 Nov 2027 — Attack the new claimant with stale completion (150m)
days.practical_task: Author and execute adversarial tests for one missing priority-claim invariant and repair only the demonstrated defect or missing regression.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Stale token 21 cannot commit after token 22 and urgent arrival does not alter already accepted operation data.
- The injected completion fault rolls back domain/audit/journey changes together.
- Valid later completion commits at most once, all work remains accounted for and no new feature is added to hide a failing invariant.

days.primary_title: Day 409 · 26 Nov 2027 — Diagnose the hidden cross-layer incident (150m)
days.practical_task: Independently diagnose an unfamiliar incident from its observed owned-history timeout and a known-good control, author a minimal reproducer and execute one falsifying counterexperiment. The selected cause is not disclosed; do not attempt a broad repair today.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Reproduce the R5 timeout on the faulty candidate and the 9 successful owned reads plus 3 safe denials on the control, using the same frozen schedule; mismatched candidate/data or a nonreproducing seed fails readiness rather than counting as a diagnosis.
- Use actual observations from at least two independent sources to identify the responsible boundary, then execute one discriminating counterexperiment that separates the diagnosis from a plausible alternative. The explanation follows observed evidence rather than a disclosed fault label.
- Account for all 12 requests and resource cleanup; preserve ownership, immutable effects and atomicity. If evidence remains inconclusive, record INCONCLUSIVE with the specific missing observation; do not infer a root cause from the timeout alone.

days.primary_title: Day 410 · 27 Nov 2027 — Verify one incident repair under matched load (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one minimal repair for the diagnosed day 181 fault and compare it with the failing candidate under the same frozen schedule.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The original minimal reproducer fails before the change and passes afterward for the diagnosed mechanism.
- Raw latency, failures, row/task counts and cleanup are reported for both candidates; unchanged or worse timing is not hidden.
- Owner denial, bounded resources and atomic durable identities remain intact; if cause was unresolved, execute a discriminating experiment and retain INCONCLUSIVE instead of inventing a repair.

days.primary_title: Day 411 · 28 Nov 2027 — Execute the timed reliability design mock (150m)
days.practical_task: Perform a timed SQL/reliability mock by implementing a tiny claim predicate, challenging it with a late-worker counterexample, then testing one lesson from the debrief.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The predicate claims at most one eligible job, excludes b and preserves deterministic order on a/c under the chosen documented rule.
- Old token 30 cannot commit token-31 work; rollback of a claim retains durable eligibility.
- Run the new debrief regression and record timed/assisted scope; no universal mastery or production guarantee is inferred.

days.primary_title: Day 412 · 29 Nov 2027 — Demonstrate the verified Block B recovery slice (150m)
days.practical_task: Run the already-prepared bounded local rollback/recovery demonstration and reconcile the displayed claims with exact observed evidence; implement no new feature.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Actual running candidate and schema after rollback match the retained manifest and A/B authorization checks pass.
- Recovered content/relationships are claimed only with matching day 154 physical restore plus day 153 retained-key proof; absent proof remains BLOCKED/NOT_RUN and cannot be replaced with an ephemeral-key round trip.
- Operation reconciliation creates no duplicate effect; every displayed performance/recovery claim points to actual bounded evidence or an explicit limitation, including assisted work and unresolved faults.

days.primary_title: Day 413 · 30 Nov 2027 — Specify a safe support-topic decision (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a three-way topic-suggestion decision table plus ABSTAIN for a human-reviewed support triage task; keep eligibility, pricing, coverage and payment decisions outside its output.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The three in-scope examples have the prescribed labels and still require human review.
- Empty or prohibited advice requests abstain with explicit reason codes.
- Output rejects all business-mutation fields and invokes zero provider, decrypt or domain-write operations.

days.primary_title: Day 414 · 01 Dec 2027 — Author the experimental label rubric (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a label-rubric validator that keeps single-intent topic labels separate from ambiguous and prohibited requests.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All three unambiguous examples retain labels; unknown label PAYMENT_APPROVED is rejected.
- The conflicting annotations produce an adjudication-needed receipt and abstention.
- Rubric changes require a new version and never rewrite a frozen labeled record.

days.primary_title: Day 415 · 02 Dec 2027 — Build a bounded training-eligible corpus (150m)
days.practical_task: Author the deterministic corpus builder from a learner-written matrix of twelve template families and three topic intents, preserving group, entity and label provenance.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Expansion yields exactly 216 unique example IDs and 72 rows per known label, with every row mapping to one group and fictional entity.
- The forbidden operational row is rejected even though its content is synthetic.
- Two builds using the same templates produce identical ordered bytes; template text cannot contain the target label or split name.

days.primary_title: Day 416 · 03 Dec 2027 — Seal source-group evaluation partitions (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a split allocator and overlap checker using source/template groups rather than row-level shuffling.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Known row counts are train 144/development 36/test 36, with six unknowns in development and six different unknowns in test.
- Any G11/G12 training member or cross-split normalized duplicate fails validation.
- All transformations fitted later are restricted to training rows; the test manifest can be hashed without opening test labels for tuning.

days.primary_title: Day 417 · 04 Dec 2027 — Implement the deterministic topic baseline (150m)
days.practical_task: Write a small keyword baseline with explicit conflict and no-match abstention; evaluate it only on training examples and a tiny development smoke set.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Single-intent examples map exactly to their expected topics.
- Conflicting keywords, no keyword and empty input abstain rather than pick the first match.
- Reordering keywords cannot change results and inference performs no external calls or domain writes.

days.primary_title: Day 418 · 05 Dec 2027 — Compute honest selective-classification scores (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement confusion counts, abstention coverage and selective error with explicit denominators for the baseline.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The result reproduces all supplied exact fractions without excluding failed cases from totals.
- An all-abstain prediction set reports selective error as undefined with denominator 0, not 0% error.
- Unknown cases are reported separately and cannot improve known-label accuracy by denominator substitution.

days.primary_title: Day 419 · 06 Dec 2027 — Regress metric denominator edge cases (150m)
days.practical_task: Add mutation-resistant tests for dropped predictions, duplicated examples and all-abstain groups in the metric calculator.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Each missing, duplicate or extra-ID batch fails completeness before computing a promotable score.
- Six valid abstentions retain total 6 and selective-error denominator 0.
- An empty batch yields NO_EVALUATION and cannot pass a release gate; each seeded metric mutation is killed by a learner-written test.

days.primary_title: Day 420 · 07 Dec 2027 — Predeclare an abstention threshold search (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a development-only threshold evaluator over fixed confidence scores and select by an explicit safety-first rule.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Threshold.50 fails because it accepts the unknown.60 and wrong.70; .75 accepts the two correct examples and is selected over.90 for greater coverage.
- A split tag TEST is rejected by the tuning function.
- An infeasible gate returns KEEP_BASELINE with actual counts rather than loosening thresholds after results.

days.primary_title: Day 421 · 08 Dec 2027 — Expose uncertainty from tiny evaluations (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a grouped bootstrap summary of a fixed prediction table without converting uncertainty into a model-quality claim.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Observed error is 4/12 and repeated seed 17 runs produce the same 200 estimates.
- Every resample contains whole groups; no individual row resampling masquerades as group independence.
- Intervals are explicitly exploratory for four synthetic groups; an all-correct result never claims zero future error.

days.primary_title: Day 422 · 09 Dec 2027 — Audit class imbalance and failure costs (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a cost-aware comparison of a majority-topic baseline and a more selective predictor on an imbalanced synthetic slice.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- M accuracy 24/30 and cost 6 are shown beside zero A/O recall; S accuracy 24/30 and cost 1.5 are not conflated with M.
- Accepted prohibited requests fail independently of aggregate cost or accuracy.
- Reports preserve minority denominators 3 and do not weight away safety failures.

days.primary_title: Day 423 · 10 Dec 2027 — Diagnose a disguised template leak (150m)
days.practical_task: Locate and repair a seeded split-audit defect that hashes raw strings but misses punctuation and case variants across partitions.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The disguised repeated template is flagged before fitting or scoring.
- Resolved and unresolved remain different; normalization does not erase negation.
- The learner explains the observed defect and records split version invalidation; no leaked score remains promotable.

days.primary_title: Day 424 · 11 Dec 2027 — Freeze a candidate-blind evaluation gate (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement an evaluation specification validator that freezes dataset, group split, metrics, thresholds and forbidden outputs before model results exist.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Complete pre-result specification validates and emits a content digest.
- Each missing or altered required input produces a non-promotable result.
- Any changed threshold creates a new protocol version and requires an untouched future holdout, never a retrospective pass.

days.primary_title: Day 425 · 12 Dec 2027 — Bound CPU experiment readiness (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement and execute a resource preflight for the chosen small text-classification experiment, without training the full candidate yet.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- A real ten-text fit/predict is recorded with elapsed time and tool version if the approved runtime exists.
- Missing dependency, unsupported resource observation or exceeded resource ceiling is explicitly blocked/narrowed, never a simulated PASS.
- No external service, private data transfer or dependency upgrade occurs; the main 144-row fit is left to its own primary.

days.primary_title: Day 426 · 13 Dec 2027 — Verify a locked dataset release (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a dataset release checker that reproduces corpus/split digests and validates rubric, license and training eligibility records.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Rebuilt 216 known rows and 12 unknown rows match the frozen ordered content and partition digests.
- Missing eligibility/license decision or changed frozen test labels blocks release.
- Operational synthetic tables are absent from allowed inputs; absent real preflight evidence leaves training NOT_READY, not implicitly verified.

days.primary_title: Day 427 · 14 Dec 2027 — Fit training-only text features (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement the feature pipeline fit/transform boundary with a training-fitted vocabulary and explicit empty-document behavior.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The 144-row training transform has a recorded vocabulary size and stable feature ordering.
- DEV_ONLY_CANARY and TEST_ONLY_CANARY are absent from the training vocabulary; unseen-only text transforms without refit.
- An empty training corpus fails explicitly, and blank inference text reaches ABSTAIN rather than causing a false confident suggestion.

days.primary_title: Day 428 · 15 Dec 2027 — Train the real CPU topic classifier (150m)
days.practical_task: Fit one real MultinomialNB classifier with alpha 1.0 on the frozen 144 training rows and save its fitted parameters with the feature configuration.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The fit consumes exactly 144 allowed training rows and produces parameters for exactly three known topics.
- Receipt records actual runtime/version, fit duration, dataset/split digests and resource observation; no fixture-only result passes the training requirement.
- Empty text is handled by the guard; fit exceeding the 2-minute/512MiB teaching limits stops safely and remains incomplete without silently changing data or model.

days.primary_title: Day 429 · 16 Dec 2027 — Evaluate trained predictions on development (150m)
days.practical_task: Run the trained classifier on the 42-row development partition and compare its errors with the frozen rule baseline using the common metric code.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Both predictors are scored on the identical 42 IDs and missing predictions fail completeness.
- Per-class errors, unknown accepted count, abstentions and denominators are visible even when the model is worse.
- No test labels are opened or used to choose a change; actual runtime and candidate identity accompany predictions.

days.primary_title: Day 430 · 17 Dec 2027 — Classify errors without tuning the holdout (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement an error-taxonomy annotator for at most twelve development failures and test that each explanation is traceable to actual predictions.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Every annotation joins to a real prediction or explicitly labeled challenge probe.
- A fabricated prediction ID and an unsupported explanation are rejected by validation.
- No corrective example is injected into training/test during this task, and challenge results are separate from held-out estimates.

days.primary_title: Day 431 · 18 Dec 2027 — Reconstruct the fitted pipeline contract (150m)
days.practical_task: Rebuild the vectorizer/classifier composition from its public contract and blank composition seam, then compare predictions with the frozen candidate.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- A fresh real fit reproduces the reference class order and all declared smoke predictions under the pinned runtime.
- A swapped class-order mutation is detected even when score values are unchanged.
- Vocabulary cannot grow during prediction; assistance or copied implementation downgrades the evidence to guided rather than independent.

days.primary_title: Day 432 · 19 Dec 2027 — Compare one bounded smoothing alternative (150m)
days.practical_task: Train exactly one alpha 0.5 alternative against alpha 1.0 and compare development results under the frozen cost and safety criteria.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Only alpha differs, both candidates use the same data and preprocessing digests.
- Actual errors/coverage/unknown acceptance and resource costs are compared; no improvement is presumed.
- Candidate selection uses development evidence only; failed hypothesis retains A or the rule baseline without reopening test labels.

days.primary_title: Day 433 · 20 Dec 2027 — Lock a development-selected abstention policy (150m)
days.practical_task: Apply the predeclared threshold search to the chosen real candidate and freeze the selected threshold or reject the candidate.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Every threshold is evaluated over the same 42 development IDs and exact denominators are retained.
- No feasible threshold yields REJECT/KEEP_BASELINE rather than threshold relaxation.
- The selected threshold and feature/model digests are frozen before the locked test is evaluated; scores are not advertised as calibrated confidence.

days.primary_title: Day 434 · 21 Dec 2027 — Run the untouched topic holdout once (150m)
days.practical_task: Evaluate the frozen model-plus-abstention policy and the rule baseline on the untouched 42-row test partition, emitting a pass/reject result without tuning.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Candidate, threshold, split and label digests match the pre-result freeze; all 42 rows are accounted for.
- Hard failures or missed teaching thresholds reject promotion, including a better average score with accepted unknowns.
- Results are labeled synthetic held-out experiment evidence, not real-user accuracy or production competence; no same-test retuning is performed.

days.primary_title: Day 435 · 22 Dec 2027 — Build an authorized extractive baseline (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a read-only extractive help baseline that filters source eligibility before ranking and returns an exact source span or abstention.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Visitor receives only public S1, A may receive authorized S2, and B receives no S2 text or metadata.
- Stale S4 and private S3 are excluded before ranking; forbidden access causes zero decrypt calls.
- Unanswerable coverage/payment questions abstain; no authority, provider or audit/journey state is mutated.

days.primary_title: Day 436 · 23 Dec 2027 — Test ranking against independent relevance labels (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement and evaluate a bounded lexical ranker on the authorized baseline corpus with learner-authored relevance labels.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Authorized relevant IDs rank with the stated stable tie rule, and metrics show query-specific denominators.
- No-relevant queries are labeled unanswerable and handled separately, not assigned convenient perfect recall.
- B-private, stale and denied sources stay excluded irrespective of lexical score; top-k never exceeds 2.

days.primary_title: Day 437 · 24 Dec 2027 — Measure actual local train and predict costs (150m)
days.practical_task: Run matched bounded repetitions of the selected small-model fit/predict path and the deterministic topic baseline, recording failures and resource limits.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- All 3 post-warmup runs use identical candidate/data/config and count every attempted prediction.
- Timeout/resource-limit cases remain in the receipt and stop further unsafe workload growth.
- Memory high-water semantics and no-billing status are explicit; estimates are not reported as provider invoices or production capacity.

days.primary_title: Day 438 · 25 Dec 2027 — Verify one available inference runtime (150m)

- Retained entry count never exceeds20 under the tested insertion sequence.

- No eviction triggers domain mutations or stores private content in persistent browser storage.

days.primary_title: Day 557 · 22 Apr 2028 — Compare old and new read projections (150m)
days.practical_task: Run a shadow comparison of the old/new visibility query against a bounded shared dataset without changing active reads.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Unaffected active rows match in identity and text.
- All intentional withdrawal/redaction differences are accounted for.
- Any unexplained difference blocks promotion; shadow work does not mutate policy/source data.

days.primary_title: Day 558 · 23 Apr 2028 — Exercise withdrawal during refresh (150m)
days.practical_task: Diagnose and repair one disclosed ordering mechanism in the source-refresh/withdrawal interaction.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The current permitted source state matches authoritative generations rather than message arrival order.
- V2 content cannot become current after withdrawal through a stale refresh.
- P1 historical binding remains unchanged and no browser event is treated as authority.

days.primary_title: Day 559 · 24 Apr 2028 — Block unsafe visibility rollback (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a release gate that refuses an older explorer build unable to represent withdrawn sources safely.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Unsafe permissive old build is rejected even if its binary starts successfully.
- Safe compatible candidate may proceed through the bounded local rehearsal.
- No rollback deletes withdrawal/audit/history records to make the old build pass.

days.primary_title: Day 560 · 25 Apr 2028 — Triage a mixed-version incident (150m)
days.practical_task: Reproduce and repair one disclosed-mechanism incident where the UI candidate and source-generation projection disagree.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Identifies the actual version mismatch from evidence.
- Containment fails closed for unrepresentable withdrawal instead of showing active content.
- No speculative fix changes policy bindings or deletes source history.

days.primary_title: Day 561 · 26 Apr 2028 — Trace one request across layers (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement or use a minimal request-trace correlation check for the incident without adding sensitive payload logging.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Correlates only R17 receipts and reports the missing stage.
- Does not infer successful SQL completion from an earlier HTTP receipt.
- Forbidden marker bytes stay absent from trace outputs.

days.primary_title: Day 562 · 27 Apr 2028 — Diagnose a visibility-update deadlock (150m)
days.practical_task: Find a seeded lock-order defect in a disposable two-transaction source-status fixture.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Captures the database deadlock/failure rather than relying on a timing guess.
- Consistent lock ordering or justified narrow redesign removes the supplied cycle.
- Retry is bounded and does not duplicate required audit/state effects.

days.primary_title: Day 563 · 28 Apr 2028 — Recover interrupted source comparisons (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement one recovery decision for read-only comparison work interrupted after source loading.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Uncommitted read-only computation can be safely recomputed under current authorization.
- Exact committed result is reused only when identity/generation still match.
- The synchronous branch does not claim durable work recovery or create a queue solely for this lesson.

days.primary_title: Day 564 · 29 Apr 2028 — Restart without stale comparison state (150m)
days.practical_task: Execute a bounded local restart test for the existing explorer release and its pinned source data.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Backend reloads authoritative current source state rather than trusting stale process cache.
- Private browser data is not persisted or restored across the session boundary.
- Any resumed read rechecks authorization/generation and produces no domain mutation.

days.primary_title: Day 565 · 30 Apr 2028 — Verify encrypted incident restore (150m)
days.practical_task: Run one bounded restore of the existing authorized encrypted snapshot and implement the readiness comparison against a separately retained current source/access-revocation manifest.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Claim positive recovery only when actual retained-key proof and restored payload/business relationships match SNAP-D337; A’s authorized read succeeds, while B and revoked Support S are denied before decrypt.
- The disposable missing-key resolver fault returns KEY_UNAVAILABLE, produces no plaintext/key marker and never alters retained recovery material; empty data is not a successful restore.
- Restored source/auth state must match the separately retained current generation9/5 control manifest. The stale generation8/4 fixture stays not-ready and serves no withdrawn source or revoked private access until authoritative current revocations are re-established and verified; no silent reactivation or permission reset.

days.primary_title: Day 566 · 01 May 2028 — Measure incident failure accounting (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement and execute a request-accounting check over a bounded degraded explorer workload.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Outcome counts sum to20 with no lost or duplicate request IDs.
- Reports latency denominator and excluded failures explicitly.
- Cannot improve reported latency by silently dropping timeout/denied outcomes or claim reliable tail percentiles from20 requests.

days.primary_title: Day 567 · 02 May 2028 — Diagnose a source-grounded answer regression (150m)
days.practical_task: Evaluate the existing read-only assistance path after source withdrawal using a locked candidate and dataset.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Withdrawn/unsupported/foreign cases meet the predeclared abstention/privacy rules.
- Historical allowed V1 questions preserve exact citations.
- Reports actual versus simulated inference honestly and never tunes on the held-out answers during this task.

days.primary_title: Day 568 · 03 May 2028 — Isolate a cross-account cache leak (150m)
days.practical_task: Reproduce and repair a seeded private-context cache-key defect without exposing real data.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- B never sees PRIVATE_A in UI/cache/errors.
- Public source-only data can still be shared under its separate public key.
- Server authorization remains effective even with a malicious or incorrect client key.

days.primary_title: Day 569 · 04 May 2028 — Reconstruct release lineage independently (150m)
days.practical_task: Rebuild a candidate-lineage manifest from actual artifacts and execute a mismatch checker.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Matching artifacts resolve to one explicit candidate tuple.
- S7 receipt is rejected rather than mixed into R3/S8 claims.
- Missing artifact hashes/versions remain UNKNOWN/NOT_RUN and are not invented.

days.primary_title: Day 570 · 05 May 2028 — Reset private state during incident recovery (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement or strengthen one session-expiry recovery test across query, form and local UI state.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- A's private query/mutation/form state is removed before B renders.
- LateR1 cannot refill B's view.
- Only approved public route selection survives, followed by authenticated authoritative refetch.

days.primary_title: Day 571 · 06 May 2028 — Rehearse a safe degraded release (150m)
days.practical_task: Select and exercise one already-built compatible candidate during a source visibility incident.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Chooses a compatible safe fallback or holds if none exists.
- Essential existing customer journey continues while optional explorer/help is disabled.
- Does not claim external deployment, change credentials or erase retained source/audit data.

days.primary_title: Day 572 · 07 May 2028 — Test bounded dependency degradation (150m)
days.practical_task: Inject one controlled dependency slowdown and verify comparison resource containment.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Optional comparison work terminates or degrades within the declared budget.
- The essential control operation is not starved by unbounded comparison work.
- No retry storm or extra runtime service is introduced to pass the fixture.

days.primary_title: Day 573 · 08 May 2028 — Close the incident with a regression (150m)
days.practical_task: Turn the diagnosed cross-layer incident into one permanent bounded regression and rerun the matching smoke.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- The defective variant fails for the intended reason.
- The repair passes while retaining ownership, history and unavailable-state semantics.
- Incident record distinguishes observed cause, assumptions, containment and remaining risk without claiming all failures are prevented.

days.primary_title: Day 574 · 09 May 2028 — Solve a fresh Java key-design mock (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a comparison-cache key under a timed fresh prompt and run adversarial equality tests.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Data-changing differences yield distinct keys.
- Later mutation of the input list cannot change stored key semantics.
- Explains complexity/equality decisions and records all hints rather than claiming memorized work is fresh.

days.primary_title: Day 575 · 10 May 2028 — Solve a fresh SQL history mock (150m)
days.practical_task: Write and execute a latest-per-source-family query with explicit tie-breaking and visibility rules.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Returns exactly one qualifying row per family under the stated rule.
- Equal timestamps produce deterministic results.
- A withdrawn latest row does not silently authorize its content; fallback eligibility is explicitly specified.

days.primary_title: Day 576 · 11 May 2028 — Solve a frontend state-design mock (150m)
days.practical_task: Build a small executable state model for pair selection, background refetch and local expansion from a fresh prompt.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- P1 never becomes P2's current result.
- Local expansion follows the declared pair-boundary rule without duplicating server data.
- Refetch failure is truthful while existing approved data handling remains explicit.

days.primary_title: Day 577 · 12 May 2028 — Defend a measured architecture mock (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a small capacity/failure model comparing on-demand comparison with a stored-derived-result alternative.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Assumptions and measured inputs are labeled separately.
- Arithmetic accounts for misses and invalidations rather than assuming all requests hit cache.
- Chooses or rejects complexity from the modeled constraint and names a falsifying observation.

days.primary_title: Day 578 · 13 May 2028 — Regress unfamiliar unknown-outcome handling (150m)
days.practical_task: Add a fresh existing-payment regression under a new response-loss schedule to test retained system reasoning.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:

- Reconciliation posts at most one durable money effect and links the correct audit observation.
- Journey success is not inferred from analytics or an HTTP acknowledgment.

days.primary_title: Day 579 · 14 May 2028 — Defend a fresh ML evaluation choice (150m)
days.practical_task: Evaluate two supplied actual-or-explicitly-simulated candidate result sets without changing thresholds after seeing results.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:

- Reports per-slice denominators and the cost of abstention.
- Distinguishes model runtime evidence from fixture analysis and does not claim zero tested leaks proves universal safety.

days.primary_title: Day 580 · 15 May 2028 — Solve a security race-design mock (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement an authorization-generation counterexample model under a fresh interview prompt.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:
- Revoked work cannot publish private content as current.
- Unchanged authorized work succeeds.
- Explains the server-side enforcement point and why client cancellation alone is insufficient.

days.primary_title: Day 581 · 16 May 2028 — Check capacity and cost arithmetic (150m)
days.practical_task: Write a small scenario calculator for the explorer's bounded resource plan without purchasing anything.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:

- Labels monetary estimates as unavailable if no current verified price source exists.
- Does not infer production capacity or authorization to provision from the arithmetic.

days.primary_title: Day 582 · 17 May 2028 — Demonstrate a fresh full-stack variation (150m)
days.practical_task: Apply one unfamiliar allowed input variation to the existing explorer and trace its behavior through UI, API and SQL.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:

- Source identities and citation text survive encoding end to end.
- The learner can locate a failure at the correct layer rather than editing every layer speculatively.

days.primary_title: Day 583 · 18 May 2028 — Diagnose a misleading benchmark mock (150m)
days.practical_task: Find a seeded flaw in a before/after performance comparison and rerun only the corrected bounded experiment.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:

- Corrected runs use matching workload/environment/accounting.
- Reports the actual result, including no improvement, without discarding failed samples.

days.primary_title: Day 584 · 19 May 2028 — Test a reviewer usability objection (150m)
days.practical_task: Turn one opt-in review comment or labeled roleplay objection into an executable explorer usability check.
days.acceptance_contract_excerpt:

- Keyboard and focus behavior remain intact.
- Labels roleplay as roleplay and does not claim customer discovery or adoption.

days.primary_title: Day 585 · 20 May 2028 — Execute a portfolio claim checker (150m)
days.practical_task: Implement a checker binding a small set of portfolio claims to actual matching evidence.

- Assisted versus independent and simulated versus actual evidence remain distinguishable.
- Unsupported production-scale, customer-adoption or team-leadership wording is removed rather than inferred from the syllabus.

- Records all help received; mechanism-disclosed or copied solutions count as guided practice rather than independent debugging.

days.primary_title: Day 587 · 22 May 2028 — Reproduce the final candidate cleanly (150m)

- Receipts identify the actual candidate and distinguish simulated from actual runtime.

days.primary_title: Day 588 · 23 May 2028 — Model an unseen comparison filter (150m)

- Unavailable evidence is not silently counted as an unchanged or removed row.

days.primary_title: Day 589 · 24 May 2028 — Implement the final narrow variation (150m)

days.practical_task: Run a timed design/code challenge against the completed change, then test one challenged assumption.

- Records reviewer/mock identity and assistance without claiming external review occurred when it did not.
